# Parity findings ledger

Source of truth: `PARITY_FINDINGS.json` (edit with `etc/parity-findings.py`). Findings came from independent reviewers and are CLAIMS until marked otherwise: they were not deduplicated or verified when imported.

Status counts: deferred 20, false-positive 15, fixed 286, forced 4, needs-spec 16, open 291, partial 28. Severity: critical 3, high 59, medium 424, low 174.

| ID | Sev | Status | Lens | SDKs | Title |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F001 | critical | fixed | L01-value-serializer | kotlin | kotlin query-string and form-body encoder leaves & = + # / ? [ ] literal (param injection, '+' decoded as space, '#' truncates URL) |
| F002 | critical | fixed | L03-request-assembly | kotlin | kotlin query-string and form-body encoder leaves & = + # ? / : ; , [ ] @ ! $ ' ( ) * unescaped (parameter injection and data corruption) |
| F003 | critical | fixed | L12-api-bodies | kotlin | kotlin form-urlencoded body (and query) values leave & = + # / ? : @ $ , ; ! ' ( ) * unencoded: field injection and value corruption |
| F004 | high | fixed | L01-value-serializer | go | go: optional integer/number/boolean query, header and cookie params are serialized as pointer addresses ("0xc000…") |
| F005 | high | fixed | L01-value-serializer | ruby | ruby: Faraday decodes and re-encodes the built query, which collapses exploded arrays to the last value, defeats allowReserved, turns '+' into a space, and sorts params |
| F006 | high | open | L02-object-serializer | php, node, python, dart, kotlin, java, swift | Container-typed primitive responses (getInventory map<string,int32>, getMatrix array<array<int32>>) bypass the strict primitive checks in 6 SDKs |

## F001 [critical] kotlin query-string and form-body encoder leaves & = + # / ? [ ] literal (param injection, '+' decoded as space, '#' truncates URL)
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L01-value-serializer | Category: wire | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: kotlin

Kotlin's BaseApi encodes every non-allowReserved query key and value with Ktor `String.encodeURLQueryComponent(spaceToPlus = false)`, and every form-urlencoded key and value with `encodeURLQueryComponent(spaceToPlus = true)`. Ktor's default `encodeFull = false` keeps the whole URL_PROTOCOL_PART set literal: `: / ? # [ ] @ ! $ & ' ( ) * , ; = - . _ ~ +`. I ran ktor-http-jvm 3.5.0, the version pinned in the golden build.gradle.kts, on "a b&c=d#e+f/g?h[i]j". The query mode gives `a%20b&c=d#e+f/g?h[i]j...` and the form mode gives `a+b&c=d#e+f/...`. The other 11 SDKs emit `%26 %3D %23 %2B %2F %3F` for these characters. Concretely, `getPetByName("Rex", category = "cats & dogs")` goes out as `?category=cats%20&%20dogs`. The server then sees category="cats " plus an injected parameter " dogs". A value "1+2" arrives as "1 2", and a value containing '#' cuts off the rest of the query as a fragment. The form body has the same problem: `note="a&b=c"` turns into two fields. deepObject keys also keep `[ ]` literal in kotlin only (`filter[name]`), while all others send `filter%5Bname%5D`. Nothing tests this: the kotlin tests only check `category=dog` and a form value with a space. Fix by building both encoders on URLEncoder with `+`→`%20` in the query (as kotlin's own encodePathSegment and encodeQueryAllowingReserved already do), or by calling `encodeURLParameter()`. Add a BaseApiTest row that asserts `a&b=c+d #e/f?` encodes to `a%26b%3Dc%2Bd%20%23e%2Ff%3F` (query) and `a%26b%3Dc%2Bd+%23e%2Ff%3F` (form), mirrored in all 12.

## F002 [critical] kotlin query-string and form-body encoder leaves & = + # ? / : ; , [ ] @ ! $ ' ( ) * unescaped (parameter injection and data corruption)
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L03-request-assembly | Category: wire | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: kotlin

Kotlin's BaseApi percent-encodes query keys and values with Ktor's `encodeURLQueryComponent(spaceToPlus=false)` and form-urlencoded keys and values with `encodeURLQueryComponent(spaceToPlus=true)`. Both are called with the default `encodeFull = false`. In Ktor 3.5.0 that setting leaves the whole URL_PROTOCOL_PART set literal: `: / ? # [ ] @ ! $ & ' ( ) * , ; = - . _ ~ +`. I confirmed this against the kotlin golden's own ktor-http-jvm 3.5.0 jar. The string `a b&c=d+e#f?g/h:i;j,k~l*m!n'o(p)q@r$s[t]u"v%w<x` encodes to `a%20b&c=d+e#f?g/h:i;j,k~l*m!n'o(p)q@r$s[t]u%22v%25w%3Cx`. When that output goes through Ktor's own URL parser, which the transport uses via `httpClient.request(currentUrl)`, the query value `R&D=1+1 #x` becomes `/pets?name=R&D=1+1%20`. Ktor parses that as `Parameters [name=[R], D=[1 1 ]]`: the caller's value is split into a second parameter, `+` is decoded as a space, and everything after `#` is dropped as a fragment. The form body has the same defect: a nickname of `c++` is sent as `nickname=c++` and the server decodes it as `c  `. The other 11 SDKs encode `&`→%26, `=`→%3D, `+`→%2B and `#`→%23. One case is reachable from the existing fixture: kotlin sends the deepObject key `filter[color]=…` with literal brackets, while all 11 others send `filter%5Bcolor%5D=…`. Since the non-reserved encoder already keeps every reserved character, `allowReserved: true` has no observable effect in kotlin. Nothing tests this: kotlin's only exact form assertion is `nickname=a+b&tags=x&tags=y` (from a space), and no test in any language puts `&`, `=`, `+` or `#` in a query or form value. Fix: use `encodeURLParameter()`, or a hand-rolled RFC 3986 unreserved encoder like the java/rust ones, for query and form components, then add `+`↔space handling for form. Unit test (kotlin BaseApiTest and PetApiTest): getPetByName category=`R&D=1+1 #x` must produce `category=R%26D%3D1%2B1%20%23x`, and setPetPreferences nickname=`c++&x` must produce `nickname=c%2B%2B%26x`. Add the same test rows to the other 11 BaseApiTests so the escape set is locked in every language.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: None. Ktor provides encodeURLParameter, and the kotlin ValueSerializer already uses java.net.URLEncoder for path encoding.

## F003 [critical] kotlin form-urlencoded body (and query) values leave & = + # / ? : @ $ , ; ! ' ( ) * unencoded: field injection and value corruption
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L12-api-bodies | Category: wire | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: kotlin

Kotlin's BaseApi encodes every application/x-www-form-urlencoded key and value with ktor's String.encodeURLQueryComponent(spaceToPlus = true). Query values go through the same function via encodeQuery(spaceToPlus = false). Both calls leave encodeFull at its default of false, so ktor only escapes characters outside URL_ALPHABET + URL_PROTOCOL_PART. I ran it against the ktor-http-jvm 3.5.0 jar the kotlin golden pins. Input "a&b=c~d*e!f'g(h)i+j k/l:m" came out as form "a&b=c~d*e!f'g(h)i+j+k/l:m" and query "a&b=c~d*e!f'g(h)i+j%20k/l:m"; '#', '?', '[', ']', '@', '$', ',' and ';' also stay literal. The consequences: setPetPreferences(note="R&D") sends `note=R&D`, which the server parses as note=R plus a stray field D. nickname="a=b" splits the field. note="C++" arrives as "C  " because a literal '+' decodes to a space. A '#' in a query value truncates the URL into a fragment. Java uses URLEncoder, csharp Uri.EscapeDataString, python quote_plus, ruby URI.encode_www_form, node URLSearchParams, php rawurlencode, dart Uri.encodeQueryComponent, go url.Values, rust form_url_encode, swift an unreserved-only CharacterSet and elixir URI.encode_www_form. All of them percent-encode & = + #. No kotlin test sends a reserved character through a form or query value: the only form assertion, PetApiTest.kt:1098, uses spaces. Fix: pass encodeFull = true (or use encodeURLParameter) for both the form and query encoders. Then add a unit test asserting `note=R%26D%3Dx%2By` in BaseApiTest.kt, plus the same query-value row in every language.

## F004 [high] go: optional integer/number/boolean query, header and cookie params are serialized as pointer addresses ("0xc000…")
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L01-value-serializer | Category: wire | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: go

Go's Options structs hold optional parameters as pointers (`*int64`, `*float64`, `*bool`, ...). The api template passes the pointer straight to `serializeStyled` for query (api.mustache:279), header (:293) and cookie (:321) params. In `serializeStyled`, a non-slice value ends up in `stringify(value)`. `stringify` dereferences only `*string`, `*time.Time` and `*models.DateTime`, plus anything that implements fmt.Stringer, such as `*Swatch`. Everything else falls to `default: fmt.Sprintf("%v", v)`, which prints the address of a pointer. I checked with go 1.26.2: `fmt.Sprintf("%v", any(&x))` printed `0x6c3f03bcc180` for `*int64`, `*bool` and `*float64`. So an optional `limit` (integer) query param goes out as `?limit=0x6c3f...`, and an optional integer header carries an address. The other 11 SDKs send `5`, `true`, or `1.5`. Petstore has no optional non-string scalar query, header or cookie param, so no golden test reaches this. Fix by dereferencing in stringify through reflection (`rv.Kind()==Ptr → rv.Elem()`), the same way toStringSlice already does, or by dereferencing in the template. Add stringify table rows for *int64, *int32, *float64, *bool, and an optional integer query param to petstore (for example `limit` on findPetsByStatus).

Reviewer suspected this is forced: None. A pointer is go's way to express an optional field, and the serializer can dereference it, as toStringSlice already does.

## F005 [high] ruby: Faraday decodes and re-encodes the built query, which collapses exploded arrays to the last value, defeats allowReserved, turns '+' into a space, and sorts params
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L01-value-serializer | Category: wire | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: ruby

Ruby's BaseApi builds a fully encoded query string and passes the whole URL to `connection.run_request(method, url, ...)`. Faraday's `Request#url` splits off the query and runs it through `params_encoder.decode`. That is `QueryParamsEncoder`, which delegates to `Faraday::NestedParamsEncoder`. Faraday then rebuilds the query with `NestedParamsEncoder.encode` (followed by `+`→`%20`). I ran faraday 2.14.2 under Ruby 4.0.5. Input `revision=1+2/a:b&colors=red%7Cblue&tags=a&tags=b` goes on the wire as `colors=red%7Cblue&revision=1%202%2Fa%3Ab&tags=b`. Input `revision=v1.0/beta:rc1&...&a=2&z=1` gives `a=2&...&revision=v1.0%2Fbeta%3Arc1...`. This has four effects. (1) Exploded arrays, which are the OAS default for query arrays (style form, explode true), keep only the last element: `tags=a&tags=b` becomes `tags=b`. That is silent data loss. (2) allowReserved is undone, because `/ : ? [ ] @ ! $ & ' ( ) * , ; =` are re-percent-encoded. (3) A literal `+` in an allowReserved value is decoded as a space (`value.tr('+',' ')`) and sent as `%20`. (4) Params are sorted alphabetically. Ruby's tests only cover `build_query_string` and `encode_query_allowing_reserved` in isolation, so none of this shows up. The petstore spec has no exploded array query param, and no test reads the wire query for `revision`. Fix by bypassing the params encoder: give Faraday the query through a passthrough encoder whose decode returns the raw string unchanged and whose encode emits it as-is, or set the request's URI query directly. Add a DefaultApiClient unit test that sends a URL with repeated keys, a `+`, and the reserved set, then asserts the exact `env.url.query`.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: None. Faraday's params_encoder is pluggable, and a passthrough encoder keeps the bytes that build_query_string produced.
- `src/spec/resources/generated/ruby/lib/petstore/client/default_api_client.rb:67` — ::Faraday::NestedParamsEncoder.encode(params)&.gsub('+', '%20')
- `src/spec/resources/generated/ruby/lib/petstore/client/default_api_client.rb:71` — ::Faraday::NestedParamsEncoder.decode(query)
- `src/spec/resources/generated/ruby/lib/petstore/client/default_api_client.rb:142` — response = connection.run_request(method.downcase.to_sym, url, serialized_body, merged)
- `src/spec/resources/generated/ruby/lib/petstore/client/api/base_api.rb:228` — v.map { |val| "#{encoded_key}=#{encode_query_value(val, allow_reserved)}" }
- `src/main/resources/templates/ruby/default_api_client.mustache:66` — ::Faraday::NestedParamsEncoder.decode(query)

## F008 [high] python format:byte MODEL fields (pydantic Base64Bytes) reject/corrupt raw bytes on construction and decode malformed base64 leniently
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L02-object-serializer | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: python

Every python model property with format: byte (PetPassport.thumbnail/scans/biometricChip, BinaryVault.seal/shards/labels) is typed pydantic `Base64Bytes`. Base64Bytes VALIDATES its input by base64-decoding it, including when the caller passes raw bytes to the constructor or assigns them (validate_assignment=True). Verified with pydantic 2.12.5: `V(seal=bytes([0,0xFF,0x10,0x42]))` raises ValidationError ('Invalid base64-encoded string'); `V(seal=b'hello world')` raises 'Incorrect padding'; `V(seal=b'test')` silently stores b'\xb5\xeb-' and serializes as "test" (the wire carries the caller's raw bytes as if they were base64); re-assigning a decoded value (`m.seal = m.seal`) raises. In the other 11 SDKs a byte field holds RAW bytes in memory and the serializer base64-encodes them (go test TestByteField_ScalarRoundTripsThroughBase64 constructs raw {0x00,0xFF,0x10,0x42}). On decode, Base64Bytes uses non-validating `base64.b64decode`: '!!!!' -> b'' and 'dG!VzdA==' -> b'test' and 'dGVz dA==' -> b'test' are accepted. This contradicts AGENTS.md Resolved 'python ... reject malformed base64 on decode (b64decode(validate=True))' — that fix only covers ObjectSerializer._deserialize (bare bytes / containers), not model fields. The python tests in TestByteFormatBase64RoundTrip claim to cover 'PetPassport.thumbnail' but only exercise ObjectSerializer.serialize(bytes), never the model field, which is why this is uncaught. Fix: a custom Annotated[bytes, PlainValidator(strict b64decode(validate=True) only for str input; pass bytes through), PlainSerializer(b64encode, when_used='json')] alias like OffsetDateTime/JsonNumber in _types.py.

## F009 [high] Request timeout does not cover the response body read in java and dart, though TransportOptions documents it as end-to-end
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L04-transport | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): False
- SDKs: java, dart

TransportOptions.getTimeout() is documented as an 'End-to-end request timeout... Covers the entire request lifecycle: connection, TLS handshake, sending the request body, and reading the response'. In java the only deadlines are HttpClient.connectTimeout and HttpRequest.timeout. The JDK cancels the request timer once response headers arrive, so a server that sends headers and then stalls the body is never timed out. I verified this on JDK 22 with a 1000 ms timeout: a server sending headers plus 3 of 100 body bytes and then sleeping 8 s made send() block for 8098 ms and fail with IOException('fixed content-length: 100, bytes received: 3'), which surfaces as NetworkException, not NetworkTimeoutException. If the server never closes, it hangs forever. dart has the same gap. Future.timeout wraps only _httpClient.send(), which completes on headers. streamedResponse.stream.toBytes() has no deadline, and dart:io HttpClient has no read timeout (only connectionTimeout is set). The other 10 bound body reads: kotlin socket/request timeout, csharp HttpClient.Timeout over the buffered content, python urllib3 read timeout, ruby read_timeout, php timeout+max_duration, node AbortSignal over arrayBuffer(), go Client.Timeout, rust reqwest timeout, swift timeoutIntervalForRequest/Resource, elixir receive_timeout+Task. Unit tests cannot see this. It needs a fixture route that sends headers then stalls the body (e.g. a chasm 'slow-body' endpoint) and a per-language assertion of NetworkTimeoutError within the timeout.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: None. java can impose a deadline with sendAsync().get(timeout)/orTimeout on the whole body future, and dart can apply .timeout() to stream.toBytes().

## F010 [high] caCertPath pins to the custom CA in most SDKs but only ADDS it to the system roots in rust, dart and ruby
- Status: **partial** (done in dart, ruby, rust; still open for php) | Lens: L04-transport | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): False
- SDKs: rust, dart, ruby, php

java (custom-only KeyStore; doc: 'an SSLContext trusting only the given CA certificate'), kotlin, csharp (CustomRootTrust), go (x509.NewCertPool), swift (SecTrustSetAnchorCertificatesOnly(true)), python (urllib3 skips load_default_certs when ca_certs is set), node (tls 'ca' replaces the roots) and elixir (cacertfile) trust ONLY the configured CA. Three SDKs keep the system roots as well. rust calls reqwest add_root_certificate, which adds to rustls native roots. dart uses SecurityContext(withTrustedRoots: true) then setTrustedCertificates. ruby sets f.ssl.ca_file, but faraday-net_http's configure_ssl always sets http.cert_store to OpenSSL::X509::Store.new.tap(&:set_default_paths) unless ssl[:cert_store] is given (checked in upstream source). So a certificate from any public CA, or a MITM CA in the OS store, is accepted by rust/dart/ruby but rejected by the other SDKs for the same config. php (Symfony 'cafile' -> CURLOPT_CAINFO) may also keep libcurl's compiled-in CAPATH; that needs a check. The TransportOptions doc ('in addition to (or instead of) the system trust store') hides the split. A fixture test would need a server with a cert from a CA in the system store but not the configured CA.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: None. rust: tls_built_in_root_certs(false). dart: SecurityContext(withTrustedRoots: false). ruby: pass ssl: { cert_store: store built only from ca_file }.

## F011 [high] csharp drops a multipart body (and a binary body's Content-Type) on a 307/308 redirect, and throws for a Stream body
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L04-transport | Category: wire | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: csharp

BaseApi hands multipart uploads to DefaultApiClient as a Dictionary<string, object>. In the redirect loop, the follow-up request rebuilds content only for byte[] and string. A Dictionary (multipart) or any other object falls through with next.Content == null, so a 307/308 replays the POST/PUT with NO body. That is a silent loss of the upload. For a byte[] body, the replay uses new ByteArrayContent(bytes2) without the declared Content-Type: mergedHeaders' Content-Type is skipped and never reapplied, so the redirected binary upload carries no Content-Type. A Stream body (what ExtractBinaryPart can return for octet-stream/image uploads) throws ApiException('Cannot replay a streaming request body...'). java buffers InputStream/File and replays them, and python/ruby/php/node/rust/elixir/go/swift replay pre-serialized bytes. A fixture test would need a 307 from a multipart endpoint, since chasm already serves 307s.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: None. Build the HttpContent once into a buffered byte[] (multipart via ReadAsByteArrayAsync, Stream via CopyTo) and re-create it with its Content-Type on each hop.

- `src/spec/resources/generated/csharp/src/PetstoreClient/DefaultApiClient.cs:569` — else if (nextBody is Stream)

## F012 [high] swift (Apple) routes only same-scheme traffic through the proxy; https targets bypass an http:// proxy
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L04-transport | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True

## F014 [high] swift transport is stateful: URLSessionConfiguration.default stores and replays cookies and serves responses from URLCache
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L04-transport | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: swift

The main session uses URLSessionConfiguration.default, whose defaults are httpCookieStorage=HTTPCookieStorage.shared, httpShouldSetCookies=true, urlCache=URLCache.shared and requestCachePolicy=.useProtocolCachePolicy. So swift silently keeps every Set-Cookie and replays it on later requests (process-wide, shared with the app), and can answer GETs from the HTTP cache without reaching the server. The noRedirect session (.ephemeral) also keeps an in-memory cookie jar. csharp explicitly sets UseCookies=false, noting 'The other 11 SDKs are stateless by default'. java/kotlin/python/ruby/php/node/dart/go/rust/elixir install no cookie jar or cache. Two identical calls can differ on the wire, and the second may never hit the server.

## F015 [high] dart BasicAuthenticator puts the raw password (and username) into its ArgumentError via ArgumentError.value, so the secret shows up in toString() and logs
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L06-simple-auth | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: dart

When the Basic credentials fail validation (CR/LF/NUL in the username or password, or ':' in the username), dart throws `ArgumentError.value(_password, 'password', msg)`. Dart's `ArgumentError.toString()` appends `Error.safeToString(invalidValue)`, which gives `Invalid argument (password): Basic auth password must not contain CR, LF, or NUL characters: "s3c\u0000ret"`. The value is also public as `e.invalidValue`. So any log line or crash report that prints the error contains the plaintext password. The other 11 SDKs throw message-only errors that never include the credential. The authenticators promise that secrets never leak into logs, and this breaks that promise. The same pattern exists nearby: `OAuth2ImplicitAuthenticator.setAccessToken` throws `ArgumentError.value(token, 'token', ...)`, which leaks the access token, and `abstract_api_client` throws `ArgumentError.value(value, 'headers', ...)`, which leaks a header value that can be an API key or token. Fix: use `ArgumentError(msg)` or `ArgumentError.value('***', name, msg)`. Unit test: in dart/test/basic_authenticator_test.dart, assert that `e.toString()` does not contain the password for the NUL-password case.

## F016 [high] OIDC rediscovery after Cache-Control max-age discards the exchanged delegate — every call after expiry throws 'Must call exchangeCode()'
- Status: **open** | Lens: L07-oauth-oidc | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: java, kotlin, csharp, php, python, ruby, node, dart, go, rust, swift, elixir

When the discovery cache expires (default 86400 s, or the OP's max-age — e.g. Google sends max-age=3600, Auth0 max-age=15), getDelegate/resolveDelegate builds a brand-new OAuth2AuthorizationCodeAuthenticator (tokenExchanged=false, empty token manager) and replaces the old one. All access/refresh token state and the exchanged flag are lost, so the next getAuthHeaders throws the 'Must call exchangeCode() before making API requests' precondition error (rust/swift CodeNotExchanged). With max-age=0 the very first API call after exchangeCode fails. Rediscovery should only refresh endpoints (or carry the token manager/exchanged state over), not reset the session. Aggravated by discovery not being single-flight outside java/go (kotlin, python, node, dart, swift, csharp, php, ruby race and can create several delegates). No language has any test of max-age parsing or rediscovery (grep for max-age in every OpenIdConnectAuthenticator test returns 0), which is why this survived.

## F017 [high] Refresh grant omits client authentication and the 'fallback' re-sends the same refresh grant (auth-code, OIDC, password BODY mode) — flows break permanently at first expiry against confidential-client OPs
- Status: **fixed** (done via decision D02 in all SDKs (batches 5-6, branch parity/spec-expansion)) | Lens: L07-oauth-oidc | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: java, kotlin, csharp, php, python, ruby, node, dart, go, rust, swift, elixir

Uniform defect (not a parity split, but in-lens and not recorded in AGENTS/PARITY_TODO). Once a refresh_token exists, the password authenticator (and always the auth-code authenticator / OIDC delegate) builds params = {grant_type=refresh_token, refresh_token=X} with NO client_id/client_secret and passes that as the 'original grant' to the token manager. The manager's internal refresh copies client_id/client_secret only from `params`, so the refresh POST carries no client authentication in BODY mode (auth-code has no BASIC option at all, so it is always unauthenticated). RFC 6749 §6 requires a confidential client (one that sent client_secret in the code/password exchange) to authenticate per §3.2.1; Keycloak/Google/Auth0 reject such a refresh (invalid_client / invalid_request). The manager then 'falls back to the original grant' — which is the identical unauthenticated refresh params — so it fails again and throws OAuth2ServerError. The password flow therefore never re-runs the password grant (unlike client-credentials, whose fallback is the real grant), and since invalidateAccessToken() never clears the refresh token there is no recovery path short of a new authenticator. The in-code comment ('RFC 6749 §6: the refresh grant carries only grant_type and refresh_token') misreads the RFC. Fix: include client_id/client_secret (BODY) on every refresh in password/auth-code, and keep the real grant params (password grant / error for auth-code) as the fallback. Test: java OAuth2PasswordAuthenticatorTest.usesRefreshTokenOnSubsequentCalls only asserts grant_type/refresh_token presence; add assertions that the refresh body carries client_id/client_secret and that a 400 invalid_grant on refresh re-runs grant_type=password.

- `src/spec/resources/generated/java/src/main/java/com/example/petstore/auth/oauth/OAuth2AuthorizationCodeAuthenticator.java:169` — params.put("refresh_token", tokenManager.getRefreshToken());
- `src/spec/resources/generated/java/src/main/java/com/example/petstore/auth/oauth/OAuth2TokenManager.java:101` — if (params.containsKey("client_id")) { refreshParams.put("client_id", ...) }  ... fetchToken(tokenUrl, params, extraHeaders);

## F019 [high] rust OIDC take_delegate() makes concurrent calls rediscover and install an unexchanged delegate (intermittent CodeNotExchanged / permanent token loss)
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L07-oauth-oidc | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: rust

rust's OpenIdConnectAuthenticator moves the delegate out of its Mutex (take_delegate) for the duration of delegate.try_auth_headers()/exchange_code().await. A concurrent call's resolve_delegate() fast path only returns early `if delegate_guard.is_some()`, so while the delegate is taken it falls through to a fresh discovery GET, builds a NEW OAuth2AuthorizationCodeAuthenticator (token_exchanged=false), stores it and then takes it → OAuth2AuthorizationCodeError::CodeNotExchanged (or ConfigurationError 'OIDC delegate is in use by a concurrent call'). If the first call restores its exchanged delegate before the second call's discovery finishes, the second call overwrites it and the session is lost permanently. The other 11 keep the delegate shared (java synchronized getDelegate, go mutex, etc.) and only the token manager serializes. Any parallel API calls through an OIDC-authenticated rust client hit this. Fix: hold an Arc<delegate> (clone the Arc out of the lock) instead of take()/restore.

- `src/main/resources/templates/rust/auth/oauth/openid_connect_authenticator.mustache:301`
- `src/main/resources/templates/rust/auth/oauth/openid_connect_authenticator.mustache:152`

## F020 [high] caCertPath adds to the system trust store in dart, rust and (likely) ruby but replaces it in the other 9
- Status: **fixed** (done via decision D72 in all SDKs (batches 5-6, branch parity/spec-expansion)) | Lens: L08-config | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): False
- SDKs: dart, rust, ruby, java, kotlin, csharp, php, python, node, go, swift, elixir

When caCertPath is set, 9 SDKs trust only that CA: java/kotlin build a KeyStore holding just the CA, csharp uses X509ChainTrustMode.CustomRootTrust, go uses a fresh x509.NewCertPool() as RootCAs, python passes urllib3 ca_certs (default certs are not loaded), node passes `ca`, php uses curl cafile, swift sets the anchor certificates with AnchorCertificatesOnly, and elixir sets cacertfile. java's own Javadoc calls this 'certificate pinning ... trusting only the given CA'. dart instead uses SecurityContext(withTrustedRoots: true) plus setTrustedCertificates, which adds the CA to the system roots; dart's own comment calls it 'TLS pinning'. rust calls reqwest add_root_certificate on a client that already has rustls-tls-native-roots, which also adds. ruby uses Faraday's net_http adapter, which always installs an X509::Store with set_default_paths, so ca_file adds to it too (inferred from the adapter; needs a runtime check). Result: with a private CA configured, dart/rust/ruby still accept any publicly-trusted certificate, for example a MITM with a public cert, while the other SDKs reject it. Same input, different trust decision. The TransportOptions doc in all 12 says 'in addition to (or instead of)', which papers over the split.

## F021 [high] go trace-context hook always receives context.Background(), so the documented OpenTelemetry setup never injects a traceparent
- Status: **deferred** | Lens: L08-config | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: go

InjectTraceContext calls the registered propagator with context.Background() every time. Go operations take no context.Context (for example GetPetById(petId, server)), so the caller's active span can never reach the propagator. The doc-comment example `otel.GetTextMapPropagator().Inject(ctx, propagation.MapCarrier(headers))` is therefore always handed a span-less Background context, and the W3C propagator writes nothing. Under the documented setup go never sends a traceparent. The other 11 SDKs read the ambient context: java/kotlin Context.current(), csharp Activity.Current, python/ruby/node/php/elixir via OTel's current context, rust Context::current(), and dart/swift callbacks that read Context.current/activeSpan. go's own tests hide the problem: withActiveSpan registers a closure that ignores the ctx argument and captures one span's ctx (`func(_ context.Context, ...) { propagation.TraceContext{}.Inject(ctx, ...) }`). That only works for a single global span, not for concurrent requests, and is not the documented usage. Go's lack of ambient context forces some difference here, but not this one: the hook advertises a ctx it can never supply. Also dead code in the same file: the unexported headerCarrier type (Get/Set/Keys) is never used, and its Get canonicalises the key while Set does not.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: Go has no goroutine-local or ambient context; the real fix needs a ctx-accepting operation variant or a documented capture pattern

## F022 [high] rust caCertPath validation cannot fail under rustls: a non-PEM file is silently ignored, and a PEM block with bad DER panics
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L08-config | Category: error-contract | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: rust

TransportOptionsBuilder::build validates the CA with reqwest::Certificate::from_pem(&pem). Cargo.toml builds reqwest with default-features=false and rustls-tls-native-roots, so default-tls is off. In that configuration from_pem just stores the bytes (`original: Cert::Pem(pem.to_owned())`) and never returns Err (checked in reqwest-0.12.28 src/tls.rs:167-174). So the 'failed to parse' InvalidCaCertificate branch is unreachable. Any readable file passes: a text file with no PEM block yields zero certs at ClientBuilder::build, the client silently falls back to the native roots, and the fail-fast promise is broken. A file with a valid PEM armour but invalid DER makes RootCertStore::add fail inside ClientBuilder::build; build_http_client then calls `.expect("failed to build HTTP client")`, which panics inside DefaultApiClient::new. That breaks the 'typed Err, never a panic' contract. The other 11 reject an unparseable CA file at construction with their built-in error (java/kotlin/dart have a garbage-PEM test for this; rust does not).

## F025 [high] java maps OAS readOnly/writeOnly to the INVERTED Jackson access mode; the other 11 ignore both keywords
- Status: **fixed** (done via decision D56 in all SDKs (batches 5-6, branch parity/spec-expansion)) | Lens: L09-models-scalars | Category: wire | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: java, kotlin, csharp, php, python, ruby, node, dart, go, rust, swift, elixir

java/models/model.mustache:692-697 renders an OAS `readOnly` property as `@JsonProperty(access = JsonProperty.Access.READ_ONLY)` and a `writeOnly` one as `Access.WRITE_ONLY`. In Jackson, READ_ONLY means the property is serialized but ignored on deserialization, and WRITE_ONLY means the reverse. That is the opposite of the OAS meaning (readOnly: appears in responses and is never sent; writeOnly: is sent and never appears in responses). I checked this with jackson-databind 2.19.4 using the golden's mapper settings. For a READ_ONLY `id` plus a WRITE_ONLY `password`, the request body is `{"id":5}`: the readOnly id is sent and the password is dropped. Decoding `{"id":7,"password":"leaked"}` gives id=null and password=leaked: the server's id is lost and a writeOnly secret is accepted. No other SDK changes behaviour. csharp/php/ruby/node only add a doc remark (csharp model.mustache:423-428, php :461-466, ruby :448-453, node :290-295). python only adds `json_schema_extra` metadata (python model.mustache:370-381). kotlin, dart, go, rust, swift and elixir have no handling at all. So java alone has wire behaviour for these keywords, and it is backwards. The petstore spec has no readOnly or writeOnly property, so nothing exercises this. Expand petstore with e.g. `Order.id: readOnly` and a `Credentials.password: writeOnly`, then pick one canonical behaviour (most likely: omit readOnly on encode, ignore writeOnly on decode, in all 12) and pin it with a round-trip test in each language.
- `src/main/resources/templates/java/models/model.mustache:692` — @JsonProperty(value = "{{baseName}}", access = JsonProperty.Access.READ_ONLY)
- `src/main/resources/templates/java/models/model.mustache:696` — @JsonProperty(value = "{{baseName}}", access = JsonProperty.Access.WRITE_ONLY)
- `src/main/resources/templates/csharp/models/model.mustache:424` — /// <remarks>This property is read-only.</remarks>
- `src/main/resources/templates/python/models/model.mustache:381`

## F026 [high] java/kotlin default optional arrays and maps to empty containers, so they send `"tags":[]` and `"location":[]`, and an absent key decodes to [] instead of null
- Status: **fixed** (done in java; still open for kotlin) | Lens: L09-models-scalars | Category: wire | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True

The kotlin default comes from BetterKotlinCodegen.toDefaultValue (lines 531-537), which returns mutableListOf()/mutableSetOf()/mutableMapOf() for every array or map. java's comes from the base java default value. The java mapper is NON_NULL and keeps empty lists; kotlin has `encodeDefaults = true` and stripJsonNulls only removes nulls. So `new Pet(name, photoUrls)` sends `{"name":..,"photoUrls":[..],"tags":[],"location":[]}`, while the other 10 send no tags/location keys. Every addPet/updatePet body carries the extra keys, and an empty array can mean 'clear this field' to a server. No java/kotlin test asserts the encoded Pet body. Fix by defaulting optional containers to null (containerDefaultToNull), and add a request-body byte assertion for a minimally-constructed Pet in all 12.

## F027 [high] python `pattern` constraint is emitted with `/.../` delimiters, so any property with a pattern rejects every value
- Status: **needs-spec** | Lens: L09-models-scalars | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: python

python/models/model.mustache:373 and :381 emit `pattern=r'{{{pattern}}}'`. CodegenProperty.pattern comes from DefaultCodegen.toRegularExpression, which is `addRegularExpressionDelimiter(escapeText(p))` (confirmed by javap on openapi-generator 7.22.0). That wraps the regex as `/<regex>/` and escapes `/`. BetterPythonCodegen extends AbstractBetterCodegen extends DefaultCodegen and does not override toRegularExpression. The model therefore gets `pattern=r'/^[a-z]+$/'`. I checked this in pydantic 2.12: with that pattern, both `abc` and `/abc/` are rejected, so every value fails, on construction and on deserializing a server response. escapeText also doubles backslashes inside the raw string (`\d`). petstore has no `pattern` property, so the golden never renders this branch. Add a pattern-constrained string property to petstore and a unit test that a matching value is accepted.

## F029 [high] java and kotlin send empty arrays/maps for optional container fields the caller never set ("tags":[], "location":[], "shards":[], "labels":{}), and add them on a decode/re-encode round-trip
- Status: **fixed** (done in java; still open for kotlin) | Lens: L10-models-composed | Category: wire | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True

Java gives optional container fields an initializer (`public List<Tag> tags = new ArrayList<>()`, `location = new ArrayList<>()`, BinaryVault `shards`/`labels`, PetPassport `scans`, StockItem `matrix`). Its mapper uses NON_NULL inclusion, which writes an empty non-null list. Kotlin does the same with `= mutableListOf()`/`mutableMapOf()` plus `encodeDefaults = true`; stripJsonNulls only removes JsonNull. So `new Pet("doggie", urls)` goes on the wire with `"tags":[],"location":[]` in java/kotlin. The other 10 leave these fields null/None/nil/undefined/absent and omit them. A GET-then-PUT round-trip in java/kotlin also turns an absent field into an explicit empty one. `location` is a positional tuple (GeoPoint), so an empty one is wrong data, and a server with minItems would reject it. The petstore mock accepts `[]` because NormalizePrefixItemsRule strips arity, so no spec catches it. Fix: null default for optional containers (containerDefaultToNull) in java/kotlin. Tests: assert the serialized body of a minimally-built Pet has no `tags`/`location` key in all 12. Expand the petstore: give an optional array `minItems: 1` so the mock rejects `[]`.

## F033 [high] getPetPhoto (content negotiation, Case 9) returns 7 different things when the server picks application/json
- Status: **open** | Lens: L12-api-bodies | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: java, kotlin, csharp, php, python, ruby, node, dart, go, rust, swift, elixir

getPetPhoto declares image/jpeg, image/png and application/json (a Photo object) for its 200 response. All 12 SDKs send `Accept: image/jpeg, image/png, application/json`, so the JSON variant is a legitimate reply. Every SDK types the return as bytes, and the bytes branch handles a JSON body differently in each one. (1) java (InputStream), csharp (Stream), ruby (StringIO) and dart (Uint8List) return the raw UTF-8 bytes of the JSON. (2) python returns the parsed dict while the signature says bytes: _deserialize returns non-bytes data unchanged when klass is bytes. (3) node returns the parsed plain object cast as Buffer (`(json) => json as Buffer`). (4) php deserializes with returnType 'string', so json_decode produces an array and settype(array,'string') yields the literal string "Array" plus an E_WARNING. (5) kotlin throws SerializationException because it calls deserialize<String> on an object. go (json.Unmarshal of an object into []byte), swift (JSONDecoder into Data) and elixir (convert_to_type(map, "binary()")) also throw SerializationError. (6) rust returns Ok with an EMPTY Vec<u8> (`_ => Vec::new()`), which is silent data loss. No SDK tests the JSON branch: the integration tests only hit the mock's default image variant, and rust's test_pet_api_get_pet_photo discards its result. Pick one contract, for example raw bytes of whatever body arrived (the java/csharp/ruby/dart behaviour) or a typed SerializationError. Then add a per-language unit test that drives getPetPhoto with Content-Type: application/json and a Photo body.

## F034 [high] go and rust send a literal `null` JSON body (with Content-Type: application/json) when the optional request body is omitted
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L12-api-bodies | Category: wire | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True

If the caller passes no Order, java, kotlin, csharp, php, python, ruby, node, dart, swift and elixir see a null body, send no entity, and strip Content-Type. go stores the typed-nil *Order in an `any` (`var requestBody any = order`). serializeBody's `body == nil` check is false for a typed nil, so json.Encoder emits `null`, and Content-Type is kept because serializedBody is non-nil. rust always calls `object_serializer::serialize(&order)` on the Option<Order>, which serde renders as `null`. Both put `POST /store/order` on the wire with a body of `null` and Content-Type: application/json, while the other 10 send an empty body with no Content-Type. Many servers reject a JSON `null` for an object schema. No SDK tests the omitted-optional-body path. Fix: go should nil-check the typed pointer before boxing (template api.mustache:352); rust should map None to body None (api.mustache:802). Add a placeOrder(nil/None) unit test to every language that asserts no body and no Content-Type.

## F035 [high] setPetAvatar application/json variant (Case 10) cannot be expressed, and selecting it puts 6+ different bodies on the wire
- Status: **fixed** (done via decision D35 in all SDKs (batches 5-6, branch parity/spec-expansion)) | Lens: L12-api-bodies | Category: api-shape | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: java, kotlin, csharp, php, python, ruby, node, dart, go, rust, swift, elixir

setPetAvatar declares image/jpeg, image/png and application/json, and the JSON variant is the object {data: format:byte, mimeType}. The generator types the body from the first content entry only (binary: InputStream/ByteArray/Stream/bytes/File/Buffer/Uint8List/*os.File/Vec<u8>/Data/binary), so no SDK can build the JSON envelope. When a caller selects requestContentType=application/json, the wire body differs by language. java's Jackson, with FAIL_ON_EMPTY_BEANS disabled, serializes the InputStream as `{}`. go json.Marshal(*os.File) also gives `{}`. kotlin (the `body is ByteArray` passthrough) and rust (the body is already bytes) send the raw bytes labelled application/json. python (b64encode), swift (JSONEncoder Data) and node (Buffer replacer) send a base64 JSON string. dart jsonEncode(Uint8List) sends a JSON int array. csharp System.Text.Json reflects over the Stream object's properties. ruby and php JSON-encode the File/SplFileObject handle. Several SDKs document 'the selector only changes Content-Type; the caller supplies a body the type accepts', but go, java, python, swift, node, dart and csharp re-encode the body, so a caller cannot even pre-build the JSON. Fix: generate one body parameter per declared content type (or a oneOf body type), or pass the body through unchanged whenever a non-binary type is selected. Then lock the wire bytes for the JSON selection in each PetApi test.

## F038 [high] php and swift put different JSON bytes on the wire ('/' escaped as '\/', php also \uXXXX for non-ASCII) and their tests were bent to hide it
- Status: **fixed** (done in php; still open for swift) | Lens: L13a-tests-transport | Category: wire | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: php, swift

php ObjectSerializer::serialize calls json_encode($sanitized, $flags) with flags 0 (or JSON_FORCE_OBJECT): PHP's defaults escape '/' as '\/' and every non-ASCII char as \uXXXX, so a pet name 'café' goes out as "café" and photoUrls as "https:\/\/...". swift's JSONEncoder is created without .withoutEscapingSlashes (available macOS 10.15+/Linux, Package.swift floor is macOS 12), so every '/' (URLs, base64 payloads) becomes '\/'. The other 10 emit literal '/' and literal UTF-8 (csharp explicitly uses UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping, python ensure_ascii=False, go SetEscapeHTML(false)). The tests diverge to match: java/kotlin/csharp/python/ruby/node/dart/go/rust/swift/elixir assert the serialized string CONTAINS the literal 'café'/'日本', but php's peer tests ('accented character serializes and decodes correctly') json_decode the output and compare the decoded value, which passes with escaping; swift's byte-array tests explicitly rewrite expectations with replacingOccurrences(of: "/", with: "\\/"). php's own query path already passes JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES (BaseApi.php:349), so the body path is internally inconsistent too. Fix: php json_encode(..., JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES|JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE|...), swift encoder.outputFormatting = [.withoutEscapingSlashes]; make php assert toContain('café')/'日本' like peers and drop swift's '\/' rewrite; add a shared 'a/b' slash-not-escaped assertion to every ObjectSerializer test.

## F041 [high] Operation-level server variants: generated variant URLs, server variables and multi-server ops are untested; elixir's R8-4 typed-variant path has no test

The petstore spec declares three operation-level `servers:` cases: getExternalPetInfo (one fixed URL), getStagingPetInfo (a templated URL whose variables have enums and defaults), and getMultiServerPetInfo (two servers, one templated). Only getExternalPetInfo is ever called, and 8 SDKs do not use the generated server type for it. java, kotlin, csharp and php pass the generated variant (`GetExternalPetInfoServer.Server0`) and assert that the requested URL starts with the spec's `https://external-api.example.com/v1`. python, ruby, node, dart, go, rust and swift pass a test-defined subclass or mock that points at the mock server, so the generated variant's URL is never checked. elixir passes a bare `%ServerConfiguration{}` and only asserts `result != nil`. ## F044 [high] Enum string literals: python/dart/php/ruby silently STRIP a single quote from the wire value; no language escapes backslash
- Status: **fixed** (done via decision D46 in all SDKs (batches 5-6, branch parity/spec-expansion)) | Lens: L14-codegen-java | Category: wire | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: python, dart, php, ruby, java, kotlin, csharp, go, rust, swift, node, elixir

AbstractBetterCodegen.toEnumValue builds every string enum value as quoteEnumValue(escapeEnumStringValue(value)). quoteEnumValue either escapes the quote character or deletes it, depending on shouldEscapeQuotationMark(). python, dart, php and ruby use a single quote and return false there, so an enum value such as `o'clock` is emitted as `'oclock'`. The rendered `{{{value}}}` is the wire value in every enum template (python/models/model.mustache:19, dart/models/model.mustache:29, php/models/inline_enum.mustache:11, ruby/models/model.mustache:20/456). Those four SDKs therefore send `oclock` and reject a server's `o'clock` as an unknown variant, while node (also single-quoted) escapes it to `\'` and the six double-quote SDKs keep it. Separately, toEnumValue never calls escapeText (upstream generators do), so no SDK escapes a backslash. A value like `a\d` fails to compile in java/kotlin/csharp, and `a\b` silently becomes a backspace. The kotlin/dart `$name` and elixir `#{}` interpolation sequences are not neutralised either. csharp is the only SDK with its own escape table (getEnumStringEscapes: \n \t \r "), and that table also omits backslash. This is latent because petstore enums contain only [a-z-] characters.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: None. Single-quoted literals can escape the quote with \' (node already does).

## F045 [high] String default literals use the comment-escaper escapeText, which mutates values and emits invalid single-quoted literals
- Status: **open** | Lens: L14-codegen-java | Category: codegen | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: ruby, php, dart, node, python, kotlin, elixir, java, csharp, go, rust, swift

Eleven toDefaultValue overrides wrap a string schema default in the target quote and escape it with DefaultCodegen.escapeText. escapeText was written for comments and double-quoted text: it turns \t, \n and \r into spaces, doubles backslashes, escapes `"` (never `'`), and then runs escapeUnsafeCharacters (`*/`→`*_/`, `/*`→`/_*`; ruby adds `=end`→`=_end` and `#{`→`\#{`). The effects differ by language. (a) ruby/php/dart/node wrap the default in single quotes but leave `'` unescaped, so a default such as `it's` is a syntax error. (b) ruby and php single-quoted strings keep `\"` literally, so the default `say "hi"` becomes the runtime value `say \"hi\"` (and ruby `#{x}` becomes `\#{x}`) and goes on the wire wrong. (c) A newline or tab in a default becomes a space in those 11 SDKs. (d) `a*/b` becomes `a*_/b` in every escapeText user. (e) kotlin `"...$x"` and dart `'$x'` interpolate, and elixir `#{}` does too. python alone uses its own escaping (`val.replace("'","\\'")`), which never escapes backslashes or newlines, so a newline breaks the literal and `\n` is reinterpreted. The same default value therefore produces different in-memory and wire values, or no compiling SDK at all, depending on language. Latent because petstore string defaults are plain words (api, v3, placed, medium, untitled).

Reviewer suspected this is forced: None. Each language needs a dedicated string-literal escaper (escapeTextInSingleQuotes exists upstream).
- `src/main/java/io/github/mridang/codegen/generators/ruby/BetterRubyCodegen.java:740` — return "'" + escapeText(String.valueOf(resolved.getDefault())) + "'";
- `src/main/java/io/github/mridang/codegen/generators/php/BetterPHPCodegen.java:630` — .map(d -> "'" + escapeText(String.valueOf(d)) + "'")
- `src/main/java/io/github/mridang/codegen/generators/dart/BetterDartCodegen.java:571` — return "'" + escapeText(String.valueOf(resolved.getDefault())) + "'";
- `src/main/java/io/github/mridang/codegen/generators/node/BetterNodeCodegen.java:566` — return getQuoteChar() + escapeText(resolved.getDefault().toString()) + getQuoteChar();
- `src/main/java/io/github/mridang/codegen/generators/python/BetterPythonCodegen.java:761` — return "'" + val.replace("'", "\\'") + "'";
- `src/main/java/io/github/mridang/codegen/generators/ruby/BetterRubyCodegen.java:820` — input.replace("=end", "=_end").replace("=begin", "=_begin").replace("#{", "\\#{")
- `src/main/java/io/github/mridang/codegen/generators/AbstractBetterCodegen.java:3927` — return input.replace("*/", "*_/").replace("/*", "/_*");

## F047 [high] Enum string literal quoting differs by language: apostrophes are silently stripped in 4 SDKs and '$' / '#{' are interpolated in 3
- Status: **fixed** (done via decision D46 in all SDKs (batches 5-6, branch parity/spec-expansion)) | Lens: L15-template-mechanics | Category: wire | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: python, ruby, php, dart, kotlin, elixir, node

toEnumValue calls quoteEnumValue. For python, ruby, php and dart, shouldEscapeQuotationMark() returns false, so every `'` is REMOVED from the enum wire value rather than escaped: `O'Brien` becomes `'OBrien'` (`value.replace(qs, "")`). node shares the `'` quote character but keeps the default escape (`'O\'Brien'`), and the 7 double-quote languages emit `"O'Brien"`. As a result, python, ruby, php and dart send a different value on the wire and fail to match the real value in responses. All four languages accept a backslash-escaped `'` inside single quotes, so stripping is not forced.

Separately, no language escapes its interpolation sigil in enum literals:
- kotlin `@SerialName("$eq")` / `EQ("$eq")` and dart `eq('$eq')` interpolate a variable, which fails to compile. Mongo-style operator enums such as `$eq` and `$in` are realistic.
- elixir `do: "#{x}"` interpolates.

The other 9 languages emit these values literally. Backslashes are not escaped anywhere either: python `'a\b'` encodes a backspace on the wire.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: None. Each language has a valid escape for its quote character (\' in all four single-quote languages, \$ in kotlin/dart, \#{ in elixir).

## F048 [high] Global server and server-variable descriptions are raw spec text placed inside string literals, so one apostrophe breaks 5 SDKs and one double quote breaks the other 7
- Status: **open** | Lens: L15-template-mechanics | Category: codegen | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: php, python, ruby, node, dart, java, kotlin, csharp, go, rust, swift, elixir

AbstractBetterCodegen.processServers puts `server.getDescription()` and `sv.getDescription()` (and `sv.getDefault()` / enum values) into the context untouched. They skip escapeText, which the operation-level CodegenServer.description does get through DefaultCodegen.fromServers. They also skip htmlUnescape, because preprocessOpenAPI handles info, tags, schemas and paths but never `openAPI.getServers()`. Every servers.mustache then writes them into a string literal with triple braces.

Which input breaks which SDK depends on the language's quote character:
- Apostrophe (`Bob's sandbox`): php, python, ruby, node and dart emit `'Bob's sandbox'`, which does not parse.
- Double quote: java, kotlin, csharp, go, rust, swift and elixir emit `"..."..."`, which does not compile.
- `$name`: interpolated in kotlin and dart.
- `#{...}`: interpolated in elixir.
- A YAML `|` multi-line description: breaks the single-line literals in python, java, kotlin, csharp, go, swift, dart and node.

I rendered `description: '{{{description}}}',` with `Bob's sandbox` and got `description: 'Bob's sandbox',`. The doc-comment copies of the same description use `{{serverDescription}}` (HTML-escaped) in 10 languages and raw in csharp and python. In csharp that raw copy sits inside an XML `<summary>` with no escapeXml, so `&` or `<` triggers CS1570 under --warnaserror.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: None. The operation-level server path already runs escapeText, and each language has a valid escape for its own quote character.

## F049 [high] go: every primary operation method's doc comment (including its `// Deprecated:` marker) is detached from the func by a blank line
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L16-docs-packaging | Category: docs | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True

In go/api/api.mustache the per-param example loop is written as a non-standalone line, `{{#allParams}}{{#vendorExtensions.pluralExamples}}` (template line 108, closing tag on line 110). Each parameter therefore emits an empty line between the doc block and `func (a *PetApi) Op(`. Go only treats a comment as a doc comment when it sits immediately before the declaration, with no blank line in between. As a result all 37 data methods in pet_api.go and store_api.go have no godoc (a scan found 37 detached of 74 API methods; the *WithHTTPInfo variants are fine). This also breaks deprecation: on FindPetsByStatus and GetPetById the `// Deprecated: This operation is deprecated.` line is detached, and it is not its own paragraph either (no `//` separator line before it). That contradicts the AGENTS.md T2-5 entry, which says go puts a `// Deprecated:` doc paragraph on EVERY public variant. The other 11 attach their operation docs and deprecation markers to the declaration.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: None. It is mustache standalone-line whitespace. Putting each section tag on its own line, and emitting `//` before `Deprecated:`, fixes it.

## F050 [high] go: golangci-lint is vacuous because every generated .go file carries the `// Code generated ... DO NOT EDIT.` marker (contradicts AGENTS 'Not vacuous')
- Status: **deferred** | Lens: L16-docs-packaging | Category: gate | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): False

All 138 .go files in the go golden, sources and tests alike, start with `// Code generated by openapi-generator-plus. DO NOT EDIT.` (from go/api_info.mustache:1). The shipped .golangci.yml is just `version: "2"`. In golangci-lint v2, `linters.exclusions.generated` defaults to `lax`, which drops every issue in a file carrying that marker (the line also matches the `strict` regex). The `golangci-lint run ./...` step in GoLintingSpec therefore checks nothing. AGENTS.md 'Known-thin gates' claims the opposite: 'Not vacuous: ... golangci adds only errcheck/ineffassign/unused on top'. AGENTS guardrail 3 records that csharp had its `// <auto-generated/>` marker removed precisely to turn analyzers on, so go is the one SDK whose linter is still turned off by a generated-code marker. The go README compounds this: it says golangci-lint 'runs staticcheck, revive, gocritic, gosec, bodyclose, errcheck', and none of those beyond the defaults are configured.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: The marker is a go convention, but `linters.exclusions.generated: disable` in .golangci.yml turns linting back on, so nothing forces the gate to be empty.

## F051 [high] kotlin: query and form-body encoder leaves & = + # ? / [ ] literal, so values split, truncate or change on the wire
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L18a-wire-request | Category: wire | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: kotlin

Kotlin encodes query keys and values, and the x-www-form-urlencoded body, with Ktor's `String.encodeURLQueryComponent(spaceToPlus=…)`. That call keeps its default `encodeFull = false`, which leaves the whole RFC 3986 reserved set literal: `: / ? # [ ] @ ! $ & ' ( ) * , ; = + ~`. I ran ktor-http-jvm 3.5.0 (the version the golden pins) on `a b&c=d+e#f?g/h~i*j!k'l(m)n,o;p:q@r[s]t$u%vé` and got `a%20b&c=d+e#f?g/h~i*j!k'l(m)n,o;p:q@r[s]t$u%25v%C3%A9` (query), and the same with `+` for space (form). Concrete effects: (1) getPetByName(category="a&b=c") sends `?category=a&b=c`, which the server reads as two parameters. (2) A `#` in any query value starts a fragment and drops the rest of the query. (3) A literal `+` (for example nickname="C++" in setPetPreferences) goes out unescaped, and a form/query decoder reads it as a space. (4) deepObject keys go out as literal `filter[k]` instead of `filter%5Bk%5D`. The other 11 SDKs escape all of these: java URLEncoder, csharp Uri.EscapeDataString, php rawurlencode, python quote, ruby CGI.escape, node encodeURIComponent, dart Uri.encodeQueryComponent, go url.QueryEscape, rust urlencoding, swift CharacterSet `-._~`, elixir URI.encode_www_form. No kotlin test sends a reserved character through the query or form path. Only the allowReserved helper and path encoding are tested (ValueSerializerTest.kt:96, :702). Fix: pass `encodeFull = true` to both helpers, or reuse the URLEncoder-based helpers the kotlin ValueSerializer already uses.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: none; Ktor exposes encodeFull=true and kotlin already ships URLEncoder-based encoders in ValueSerializer
- `src/spec/resources/generated/kotlin/src/main/kotlin/com/example/petstore/api/BaseApi.kt:485` — internal fun encode(value: String): String = value.encodeURLQueryComponent(spaceToPlus = true)
- `src/spec/resources/generated/kotlin/src/main/kotlin/com/example/petstore/api/BaseApi.kt:495` — internal fun encodeQuery(value: String): String = value.encodeURLQueryComponent(spaceToPlus = false)
- `src/spec/resources/generated/kotlin/src/main/kotlin/com/example/petstore/api/BaseApi.kt:452` — val encodedKey = encodeQuery(key)
- `src/spec/resources/generated/kotlin/src/main/kotlin/com/example/petstore/api/BaseApi.kt:229` — parts.add("${encode(key)}=${encode(objectSerializer.stringify(item))}")
- `src/main/resources/templates/kotlin/base_api.mustache:473` — internal fun encode(value: String): String = value.encodeURLQueryComponent(spaceToPlus = true)
- `src/main/resources/templates/kotlin/base_api.mustache:483` — internal fun encodeQuery(value: String): String = value.encodeURLQueryComponent(spaceToPlus = false)

## F052 [high] node skips ALL validation for nested models and model-array elements (required, type, enum, Set/Decimal coercion)
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L18b-wire-response | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: node

ObjectSerializer.deserialize validates only the top-level model. It runs plainToInstance and then `new cls(instance)`. class-transformer builds nested @Type models with a no-arg `new Category()`, so the nested constructor runs with data===undefined: required checks are skipped and the typeof/enum checks run on an empty object before the fields are assigned. I reproduced this in a scratch copy of the generated Pet/Category/Tag models with class-transformer 0.5.1. Node ACCEPTS all of these: `{"name":"x","photoUrls":[],"category":{"id":"42"}}` (string id kept), `"category":"oops"` / `5` / `[1,2]` (a raw primitive or array lands in a Category-typed field), `"tags":[{"id":"7"}]`, `"tags":"abc"`, and `"photoUrls":[1,2]`. The other 11 reject each of these with their SerializationError (java/kotlin/csharp/go/rust/swift/python/dart; ruby/elixir reject the type errors). It also means a nested Pet (PetPassport.pet) gets no required-field check (`{"pet":{}}` accepted), no unknown-enum check on `status`, keeps `photoUrls` as a plain Array instead of the declared Set (duplicates not collapsed), and keeps `weightKg` as a JS number instead of the branded Decimal string. The same response decodes to a different shape depending on nesting depth. None of the 12 test suites has a nested wrong-type test, which is why this went unnoticed.
- `src/spec/resources/generated/node/src/object-serializer.ts:563` — const instance = plainToInstance(cls, json, { excludeExtraneousValues: true, });
- `src/spec/resources/generated/node/src/object-serializer.ts:575` — const built = new (cls as unknown as new (i: unknown) => T)(instance);
- `src/spec/resources/generated/node/src/models/pet.ts:87` — if (data !== undefined) { if (this.name == null) { throw new TypeError("name is required");
- `src/spec/resources/generated/node/src/models/pet.ts:40` — @Type(() => Category) category?: Category;
- `src/main/resources/templates/node/models/model.mustache:535` — throw new TypeError('{{name}} is required');

## F053 [high] php container leaves re-json_decode already-decoded values: enum maps fail, and int/string leaves are coerced ("abc"->0, 7.5->7, "true"->"1")
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L18b-wire-response | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: php

For container return types (`Ds\Map<int>` getInventory, `Ds\Vector<Ds\Vector<int>>` getMatrix, `Ds\Vector<Ds\Map<Swatch>>` getSwatchGroups), deserializeInternal recurses into the leaves with values json_decode has already decoded. The leaf branches then treat a PHP string as JSON text and json_decode it a second time. (1) Enum leaf (line 642): a valid value "red" goes through json_decode("red") and becomes null. BackedEnumNormalizer then throws 'The data is neither an integer nor a string', so getSwatchGroups fails on every VALID payload. php has no getSwatchGroups test; only dart and node test it. (2) int leaf (lines 498-517): "5" becomes 5 (the other 11 reject a JSON string for an int, except the lax langs in the container-leaf finding). "abc" becomes intval(null) = 0. 7.5 becomes 7. true becomes 1. A nested object or array becomes 0 ('Non-scalar input falls back to 0'). (3) string/float/bool leaves use settype (line 522), so a string leaf "true" is decoded to bool and re-stringified as "1", and "null" becomes "". Model fields go through assertPrimitiveTypes and are strict, so this applies only to top-level and container primitive or enum responses.

AbstractBetterCodegen.deriveQuerySerializationKind returns "content" when a query param has `content`, and each api template handles that branch differently. java/kotlin/dart/swift go through the SDK ObjectSerializer (wire names, canonical date-times). csharp calls a bare `System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.Serialize` with default options, not the SDK's: nulls are kept and the configured date-time/number converters are bypassed. python uses `json.dumps`, which raises TypeError on any pydantic model or datetime. ruby uses `JSON.generate` (a Dry::Struct falls back to `to_s`). node uses `JSON.stringify`, which ignores class-transformer `@Expose` wire names and emits Dates with `Z`. php uses `json_encode`: php property names, and DateTime becomes an object. elixir uses `Jason.encode!`, which raises Protocol.UndefinedError on non-derived structs instead of SerializationError. go uses `json.Marshal` with the error discarded (`jsonBytes, _ :=`) and HTML escaping ON, contradicting the AGENTS 'Resolved' entry that go serializes with SetEscapeHTML(false). rust uses `serde_json::to_string(..).unwrap_or_default()`, which silently sends `param=` on error. swift uses `try?`, which silently drops the param on error. Assert the exact `q=` bytes, including `takenAt` in canonical `.SSS+00:00` form and a `<` in `caption`.

## F055 [high] OAS readOnly/writeOnly: java maps them to Jackson access modes with inverted client semantics; the other 11 only add doc comments. Petstore has no readOnly/writeOnly property
- Status: **fixed** (done via decision D56 in all SDKs (batches 5-6, branch parity/spec-expansion)) | Lens: L19-spec-coverage | Category: spec-coverage | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: java, kotlin, csharp, php, python, ruby, node, dart, go, rust, swift, elixir

java/models/model.mustache:692-697 emits `@JsonProperty(access = JsonProperty.Access.READ_ONLY)` for `readOnly: true` and `WRITE_ONLY` for `writeOnly: true`. Jackson defines these from the point of view of the serialized document. READ_ONLY means serialize but ignore on deserialize. WRITE_ONLY means deserialize but never serialize. In a client this is backwards. A server-populated readOnly field (id, createdAt) is DROPPED when java decodes the response and comes back null. A writeOnly field (password, secret) is NEVER SENT in the java request body. I checked this against jackson-databind 2.21.1 with the generator's mapper settings: a READ_ONLY field decoded from `{"r":"srv"}` is null, and serializing an object whose only field is WRITE_ONLY fails with 'no properties discovered'. Of the other 11, python/node/ruby/php/csharp emit doc or json_schema_extra only (python/models/model.mustache:373, node/models/model.mustache:290-295, ruby/models/model.mustache:448-453, php/models/model.mustache:461-466, csharp/models/model.mustache:423-428), and kotlin/dart/go/rust/swift/elixir ignore the keywords. All 11 send and receive both kinds of field normally. The petstore and probe specs declare no readOnly/writeOnly property, so no golden or test notices. Proposed YAML (petstore components.schemas, used by a request/response op such as addPet): `Account: {type: object, required: [username], properties: {id: {type: integer, format: int64, readOnly: true}, username: {type: string}, password: {type: string, writeOnly: true}}}`, plus `/store/account: post: {operationId: createAccount, security: [], requestBody: {required: true, content: {application/json: {schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Account'}}}}, responses: {'200': {description: ok, content: {application/json: {schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Account'}}}}}}`. Assert in every SDK that the echoed `id` decodes and that `password` is on the wire.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: none: Jackson can express OpenAPI semantics only with request/response views; the plain annotation inverts them
- `src/main/resources/templates/java/models/model.mustache:692` — @JsonProperty(value = "{{baseName}}", access = JsonProperty.Access.READ_ONLY)
- `src/main/resources/templates/java/models/model.mustache:696` — @JsonProperty(value = "{{baseName}}", access = JsonProperty.Access.WRITE_ONLY)
- `src/main/resources/templates/node/models/model.mustache:290` — {{#isReadOnly}} * @readonly
- `src/main/resources/templates/csharp/models/model.mustache:424` — /// <remarks>This property is read-only.</remarks>

## F056 [high] Schema validation keywords (pattern/minLength/maxLength/minimum/maximum/multipleOf/minItems/maxItems) are enforced only by python; petstore declares none
- Status: **open** | Lens: L19-spec-coverage | Category: spec-coverage | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: python, java, kotlin, csharp, php, ruby, node, dart, go, rust, swift, elixir

python/models/model.mustache:370-381 turns every constraint into a pydantic Field kwarg (`min_length`, `max_length`, `pattern=r'...'`, `ge/gt/le/lt`, `multiple_of`, `min_length` for minItems). No other language's templates reference `{{#pattern}}`, `{{#minLength}}`, `{{#maximum}}` and the rest (grep over all 12 template trees finds only python/models/model.mustache). Python therefore rejects values the other 11 accept, both when the caller builds a model and when a server RESPONSE is decoded: an out-of-range response field is a python ValidationError/SerializationError and is accepted everywhere else. That breaks the 'same inputs accepted/rejected' rule. It also exposes python-only failures at import time. The pattern is emitted raw inside `r'...'`, so a pattern containing `'` is a SyntaxError. pydantic-core's regex engine rejects ECMA look-around, so a pattern like `^(?!admin).*$` makes the models module fail to import. The petstore spec has 0 occurrences of any of these keywords, so this never renders. Proposed YAML: add to Pet `nickname: {type: string, minLength: 2, maxLength: 8, pattern: '^[a-z]+$'}`, to Order `quantity: {..., minimum: 1, maximum: 100}`, and a probe-only `handle: {type: string, pattern: "^(?!admin)[a-z']+$"}`. Decide one cross-language policy, either enforce everywhere or nowhere (likely nowhere on the response path), and lock it with a response carrying `quantity: 500`.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: none

- `src/spec/resources/specs/petstore/openapi.yaml:1504` — Order: (no minimum/maximum/pattern anywhere in the spec)

## F057 [high] allOf inheritance with a discriminator: 6 SDKs emit class inheritance, where kotlin's `open data class` will not compile; 6 SDKs flatten; only python dispatches to the subclass. Not exercised
- Status: **open** | Lens: L19-spec-coverage | Category: spec-coverage | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): False
- SDKs: kotlin, java, csharp, node, python, ruby, go, dart, rust, swift, elixir, php

Petstore polymorphism is oneOf+discriminator (PetFood) and a discriminator-less allOf (PetWithOwner, which gets no `parent`). The classic `Pet{discriminator: petType}` + `Cat: allOf[Pet, {...}]` shape sets CodegenModel.parent/hasChildren and takes untested template paths. kotlin renders `{{#parent}}open {{/parent}}data class X(...) : Parent()`. `open` is illegal on a data class, the parent is a final data class, and the re-declared vals lack `override`, so this cannot compile. java (`extends {{parent}}`, model 522), csharp (`: {{parent}}`, 323), node (`extends`, 259), python (`class X(Parent)`, 32) and ruby (`< Parent`, 340) subclass while also flattening the parent's vars into the child. go/dart/rust/swift/elixir/php have no `{{#parent}}` at all and flatten. Only python emits `__discriminator_value_class_map` / get_discriminator_value on the parent (python model 528-533). Decoding a parent-typed response whose discriminator names a child therefore returns the child subclass in python and a bare parent, with child fields lost or rejected, elsewhere. ## F059 [high] format: time handling: php sends a full RFC 3339 date-time, kotlin has no serializer so its models will not compile, and precision is split between seconds and sub-seconds. Petstore has no format: time
- Status: **open** | Lens: L19-spec-coverage | Category: spec-coverage | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: php, kotlin, java, python, ruby, csharp, elixir, node, rust, go, dart, swift

Every codegen maps `time` (java/kotlin LocalTime, csharp TimeOnly, php \DateTimeImmutable, python datetime.time, ruby Tod::TimeOfDay, node Temporal.PlainTime, rust NaiveTime, elixir Time.t(); go/dart/swift String), but neither spec has a `format: time` field or param. Divergences found in the templates: (1) php serializes any \DateTimeInterface with DATE_TIME_FORMAT = RFC3339_EXTENDED, both in sanitizeForSerialization and in stringify. A time-of-day therefore goes out as `2026-10-15T14:30:00.000+00:00`, and php's own test only asserts `toContain('2024-01-15T10:20:30')`. (2) kotlin maps time to java.time.LocalTime but registers no contextual serializer (object_serializer.mustache:878-884), and the model template adds @Contextual only for date/date-time/uuid/uri/duration/number. A @Serializable model with a LocalTime field therefore fails to compile. kotlin's stringify also routes LocalTime into `is TemporalAccessor -> DATE_TIME_FORMATTER.format(value)`, which throws for a type with no offset. (3) Precision: python truncates to seconds (`isoformat(timespec='seconds')`), as do ruby `%H:%M:%S`, csharp `HH:mm:ss` and elixir `Time.truncate(:second)`. java ISO_LOCAL_TIME, node PlainTime (its test expects `09:15:30.25`), rust NaiveTime and dart's validated String keep the fraction, and go/swift pass any String through unvalidated. python's test comment claims 'the other 11 SDKs ... all emit HH:MM:SS', which the code contradicts. Proposed YAML: add to StockItem `opensAt: {type: string, format: time, example: '09:15:30.250'}` and a query param `at: {in: query, schema: {type: string, format: time}}` on getStockItem. Assert the wire value byte-for-byte in all 12.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: go/dart/swift String surface is arguably forced (no stdlib civil-time type); php/kotlin/precision split are not

## F060 [high] R8-1 claim false for dart: BinaryVault.labels (map of format:byte) serializes as JSON int arrays, not base64
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L20-doc-truth | Category: doc-truth | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True

AGENTS Round 8 and PARITY_TODO R8-1 say a format:byte map now goes on the wire as base64 strings in all 12 SDKs, and that dart got a per-value base64Encode. The dart golden's toJson does a plain assignment `json['labels'] = labels;` of a `Map<String, Uint8List>`. ObjectSerializer.serialize is a bare `jsonEncode(object)` with no toEncodable hook, and Uint8List is a List<int>, so the wire value is `{"labels":{"k":[1,2,3]}}`. Decoding does base64Decode, so dart cannot round-trip its own output. The template has a base64Encode map branch, but it sits under `{{^isPrimitiveType}}`; a map of byte arrays is a primitive-typed map, so the plain-assignment branch renders instead. No dart test touches BinaryVault.labels, so the R8-1 lock does not cover dart. A smaller point: php keeps the base64 wire form in memory (`\Ds\Map<string,string>` plus getLabelsAsBytes/setLabelsFromBytes), so 'native bytes in memory, in all 12' is also not literally true for php.

## F061 [high] rust OpenIdConnectAuthenticator fails concurrent requests and loses its delegate (exchanged tokens) when a call is cancelled
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L22-lifecycle | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: rust

try_auth_headers/exchange_code move the resolved delegate OUT of its Mutex (take_delegate) for the whole token-fetch await and only put it back afterwards. (1) Any second API request on the same Client that arrives during that window gets Err(ConfigurationError::InvalidState("OIDC delegate is in use by a concurrent call")). Two parallel requests through an OIDC-authenticated rust client therefore fail spuriously, where the other 11 either serialize discovery (java synchronized getDelegate, go mutex) or let both proceed. (2) Dropping the future (tokio cancellation or timeout) while awaiting leaves self.delegate = None. The next call re-runs discovery and builds a fresh OAuth2AuthorizationCodeAuthenticator, so the exchanged code's access and refresh tokens are lost and every later call fails with CodeNotExchanged. resolve_delegate also runs while another call holds the delegate and overwrites it, and the restore then overwrites again. No other language makes a concurrent caller fail. A cancelled call loses state only in rust.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: Avoiding holding a std Mutex across .await. A tokio::sync::Mutex or an Arc<delegate> (as the rust token manager already does) removes the need, so this is not forced.
- `src/spec/resources/generated/rust/src/auth/oauth/openid_connect_authenticator.rs:130` — Two concurrent calls can race for it; the loser gets [`ConfigurationError::InvalidState`].

- `src/main/resources/templates/rust/auth/oauth/openid_connect_authenticator.mustache:130` — fn take_delegate(
- `src/spec/resources/generated/java/src/main/java/com/example/petstore/auth/oauth/OpenIdConnectAuthenticator.java:82` — private synchronized OAuth2AuthorizationCodeAuthenticator getDelegate()

## F062 [high] swift OAuth2 token POSTs go through a new, never-invalidated URLSession with no proxy, and Proxy-Authorization is sent to the IdP
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L22-lifecycle | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: swift

Every noRedirect request (every OAuth2 token fetch and refresh) calls buildNoRedirectSession, which creates a brand-new URLSession with a SessionDelegate on .ephemeral config and never calls finishTasksAndInvalidate. A URLSession retains its delegate until it is invalidated, so each token fetch leaks one session, its delegate and its connection pool, and never reuses the main session's connections. The new config also never copies connectionProxyDictionary, so token requests bypass the configured proxy. sendRequest has already merged proxyAuthHeader into the request headers before choosing the session, so the proxy's Basic credentials go straight to the token endpoint. The other 11 send token POSTs through the same shared transport (go uses a context flag on the same http.Client, the rest pass a noRedirect flag to the same client), honouring the proxy and the pool, as Client/AGENTS promise ('token exchange ... use the same proxy, TLS, and timeout settings').

Reviewer suspected this is forced: URLSession has no per-task redirect switch except through the delegate. But the shared SessionDelegate already keys state per task, so a per-task noRedirect flag on the primary session is possible.

- `src/spec/resources/generated/swift/Sources/PetstoreClient/DefaultApiClient.swift:892` — return URLSession(configuration: config, delegate: delegate, delegateQueue: nil)

## F064 [medium] Path values "." and ".." pass through encodePathSegment unencoded, and some transports then resolve them as dot-segments
- Status: **open** | Lens: L01-value-serializer | Category: wire | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: node, python, dart, rust, csharp, php, java, kotlin, go, ruby, swift, elixir

In all 12 encoders, `.` is unreserved and stays literal, so `getPetByName("..")` produces `/pet/byName/..?category=x`. What happens next depends on the transport. node (WHATWG) produced `http://h/pet/?category=x`, python's urllib3 `parse_url` produced `/pet/?category=x`, and dart's `Uri.parse` produced `http://h/pet/?category=x`. In those SDKs the request reaches a different endpoint (/pet). rust (url crate, WHATWG), csharp (System.Uri) and php (Symfony resolveUrl) most likely behave the same way; those three were not run. java (java.net.URI), swift (URL) and ruby send `/pet/byName/..` literally, and go and elixir most likely do too (not run). This is a wire divergence with security weight: a user-controlled name reroutes the request. WHATWG treats even `%2E%2E` as `..`, so encoding alone cannot make node or rust agree. The uniform fix is to reject a path-segment value equal to `.` or `..` in all 12, with the language's argument error, or always encode them as `%2E` and accept that node and rust still normalize.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: Partly. node and rust go through WHATWG URL parsing, which resolves `..` and `%2E%2E`. Rejecting these values up front would be uniform.
