## F172 [medium] Digit-leading property/param names give invalid identifiers in python/dart/php/rust and an unexported (silently dropped) field in go
- Status: **fixed** (done via decision D43 in all SDKs (batches 5-6, branch parity/spec-expansion)) | Lens: L14-codegen-java | Category: codegen | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: python, dart, php, rust, go, csharp

AbstractBetterCodegen.toVarName and toParamName send any name matching ^\d to escapeReservedWord, which was written to escape keywords. The base implementation prefixes `_`, giving `_1st`, which works for java/kotlin/node/swift/ruby/elixir. python, dart and php override it to append `_`, producing `1st_`, which is a syntax error in all three (php `$1st_`). rust overrides it to prefix `r#`, producing `r#1st`, which is not a legal raw identifier. go turns off reserved escaping but the digit branch still yields `_1st`, an unexported struct field that the alias-based MarshalJSON/UnmarshalJSON (go/pkg/models/pet.go:114-125) skips, so the property is silently dropped in both directions. csharp also gets `_1st`, which its own comment says CA1707 rejects under the analyzers. A property or query parameter such as `2fa` or `1stPlace` therefore produces six different results.

## F174 [medium] Numeric default literals compile in java only: kotlin/csharp/rust/node/python emit literals that do not type-check, or corrupt them
- Status: **open** | Lens: L14-codegen-java | Category: codegen | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: kotlin, csharp, rust, node, python, java

java's toDefaultValue adds the `L` and `F` suffixes and wraps a format-less number or decimal in `new java.math.BigDecimal("...")`. The other SDKs emit the raw default verbatim, with these results. kotlin maps number to BigDecimal and float to Float, so `val x: BigDecimal? = 1.5` and `val f: Float? = 1.5` do not compile. csharp maps number to decimal and float to float, so `decimal? X = 1.5` is CS0664 (needs the `M` suffix) and float needs `f`. rust maps number to f64, so an integral default `3` gives `Some(3)` in an Option<f64>, error E0308. node maps a format-less number to the branded `Decimal` string type, so `x: Decimal = 1.5` is a TS type error. python's fixEnumDefaultValue override has no isEnum guard: it prefixes the class name onto any default containing `.` that is not a quoted string, so `default: 1.5` becomes `Defaults1.5`, which is invalid Python (the base implementation and php both check prop.isEnum). The only petstore defaults are `retries: 3` (int32) and enum or string values, so none of this is exercised.

## F175 [medium] format: uri is a validated typed URI in 6 SDKs and an unvalidated plain string in 6, despite stdlib URI types existing
- Status: **open** | Lens: L14-codegen-java | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: java, kotlin, csharp, php, python, node, dart, swift, go, ruby, rust, elixir

The typeMapping for URI differs across the 12, and so does what each SDK accepts for Pet.homepageUrl. java maps it to java.net.URI, which rejects malformed syntax on decode. kotlin uses io.ktor.http.Url, which is lenient. csharp uses System.Uri. php uses Uri\Rfc3986\Uri, and UriNormalizer throws on an invalid value. python uses UrlStr, an HttpUrl validator that also rejects relative and non-http(s) URIs such as `mailto:x` or `/a`. node uses a type-only brand with no runtime check. dart, swift, go, ruby, rust and elixir keep a plain String and accept anything. The golden shows the split: java Pet.java:124 `URI`, kotlin Pet.kt:80 `Url`, csharp Pet.cs:161 `Uri`, php Pet.php:58 `\Uri\Rfc3986\Uri`, python pet.py:46 `UrlStr`, node pet.ts:60 `URI`, versus dart pet.dart:66, go pet.go:75, ruby pet.rbs:14, rust pet.rs:50, swift Pet.swift:33 and elixir pet.ex:25, all String. dart (`Uri`), swift (`URL`), go (`net/url`), ruby (`URI`) and elixir (`URI`) all have stdlib URI types, so no language feature forces the split, and AGENTS.md does not record it.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: Partly: rust has no stdlib URL type (the url crate is external). The other five string-typed SDKs have stdlib types.
- `src/main/java/io/github/mridang/codegen/generators/java/BetterJavaCodegen.java:93` — typeMapping.put("URI", "URI");
- `src/main/java/io/github/mridang/codegen/generators/python/BetterPythonCodegen.java:144` — typeMapping.put("URI", "UrlStr");
- `src/main/java/io/github/mridang/codegen/generators/dart/BetterDartCodegen.java:118` — typeMapping.put("URI", "String");
- `src/main/java/io/github/mridang/codegen/generators/swift/BetterSwiftCodegen.java:97` — typeMapping.put("URI", "String");
- `src/main/java/io/github/mridang/codegen/generators/go/BetterGoCodegen.java:122` — typeMapping.put("URI", "string");
- `src/spec/resources/generated/php/lib/Serializer/UriNormalizer.php:65` — $parsed = \Uri\Rfc3986\Uri::parse($data);
- `src/spec/resources/generated/node/src/brand.ts:55` — export type URI = string & { readonly __brand: "URI" };

## F177 [medium] Package-manifest description is escaped differently per language: entity-encoded in 4 manifests, raw XML or raw strings in others
- Status: **open** | Lens: L15-template-mechanics | Category: codegen | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: node, php, python, rust, java, csharp, ruby, kotlin, elixir, dart

appDescription (escapeText'd info.description) reaches the published package metadata in three different ways:
- HTML-escaped `{{appDescription}}`: node package.json, php composer.json, python pyproject.toml, rust Cargo.toml. A description like `Pets & owners' API` is published to npm, Packagist, PyPI and crates.io as `Pets &amp; owners&#39; API`.
- Raw into XML: java pom.xml `<description>{{{appDescription}}}</description>` and csharp csproj `<Description>{{{appDescription}}}</Description>`. A `&` or `<` makes the XML ill-formed, so the Maven and MSBuild builds fail.
- Raw into a string literal: ruby gemspec `'...'` (an apostrophe is a syntax error, and the escapeText `\"` stays a literal backslash), kotlin `"..."` (`$` interpolates), elixir `"..."` (`#{` interpolates), and dart pubspec as an unquoted YAML scalar (`: `, a leading `&`/`*`/`#` breaks parsing, and `\"` stays literal).

The same info.description thus yields correct, entity-garbled or unbuildable package metadata depending on the language.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: Each manifest format needs its own escaping, but none of these templates applies it.
- `src/main/resources/templates/node/package.mustache:5` —   "description": "{{appDescription}}",
- `src/main/resources/templates/php/composer.mustache:3` — "description": "{{#appDescription}}{{appDescription}}{{/appDescription}}...
- `src/main/resources/templates/python/pyproject_toml.mustache:4` — description = "{{#appDescription}}{{appDescription}}{{/appDescription}}...
- `src/main/resources/templates/rust/cargo_toml.mustache:7` — description = "{{#appDescription}}{{appDescription}}{{/appDescription}}...
- `src/main/resources/templates/java/pom.mustache:8` — <description>{{#appDescription}}{{{appDescription}}}{{/appDescription}}...
- `src/main/resources/templates/csharp/csproj.mustache:5` — <Description>{{{appDescription}}}</Description>
- `src/main/resources/templates/ruby/gemspec.mustache:15` — s.description = '{{#appDescription}}{{{appDescription}}}{{/appDescription}}...
- `src/main/resources/templates/dart/pubspec.mustache:4` — description: {{{.}}}
- `src/spec/resources/generated/java/pom.xml:8` — <description>A simplified Pet Store API for integration testing.</description>

## F178 [medium] Raw tag and externalDocs prose skips escapeText, so a multi-line or '*/' description breaks compilation in some SDKs but not others
- Status: **open** | Lens: L15-template-mechanics | Category: codegen | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: go, rust, swift, dart, csharp, ruby, java, kotlin, php, node, python, elixir

injectTagMetadata stores `tag.getDescription()` and the tag externalDocs description raw. Model and operation externalDocs are raw ExternalDocumentation objects. None of them pass through escapeText, so newlines are not collapsed and the `*/` to `*_/` guard in AbstractBetterCodegen.escapeUnsafeCharacters never runs on them.

What breaks depends on the comment style:
- A multi-line tag description (a common `description: |` block) lands as `// line1\nline2` or `/// line1\nline2`. The second line is bare code, so go, rust, swift, dart and csharp fail to compile, and ruby (`# `) fails too.
- java, kotlin, php and node survive the newline inside `/** */`, but a `*/` in the same raw text closes their block comment early.
- python and elixir place it in `"""` docstrings or heredocs, where only a literal `"""` or (in elixir) `#{` breaks.

The same spec text therefore compiles in some SDKs and not in others. I rendered go's `{{#tagDescription}}\n// {{.}}` with a two-line value and got an uncommented second line.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: None. Operation notes and model descriptions are already normalised through escapeText.
- `src/main/java/io/github/mridang/codegen/generators/AbstractBetterCodegen.java:4663` — .ifPresent(desc -> operations.put("tagDescription", desc));
- `src/main/java/io/github/mridang/codegen/generators/AbstractBetterCodegen.java:3928` — return input.replace("*/", "*_/").replace("/*", "/_*");
- `src/main/resources/templates/go/api/api.mustache:74` — // {{.}}
- `src/main/resources/templates/rust/api/api.mustache:80` — /// {{.}}
- `src/main/resources/templates/csharp/api/api.mustache:89` — /// {{#lambda.escapeXml}}{{{.}}}{{/lambda.escapeXml}}
- `src/main/resources/templates/java/api/api.mustache:25` —  * {{{.}}}
- `src/spec/resources/generated/go/pkg/pet_api.go:131` — // Everything about your Pets

## F179 [medium] Spec prose is HTML-escaped by {{...}} in 5 languages' API docs and left raw by {{{...}}} in the other 7, for the same doc slot
- Status: **partial** (done in csharp; still open for dart, elixir, go, java, kotlin, node, php, python, ruby, rust, swift) | Lens: L15-template-mechanics | Category: docs | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: node, dart, go, rust, swift, java, kotlin, csharp, php, python, ruby, elixir

The main templates go through openapi-generator's MustacheEngineAdapter. It uses jmustache's default compiler, and AbstractBetterCodegen does not override processCompiler, so `{{x}}` HTML-escapes its value while `{{{x}}}` emits it raw. I checked this with jmustache 1.16: `pet's "x" a<b & c=d` renders as `pet&#39;s &quot;x&quot; a&lt;b &amp; c&#x3D;d`. Only renderOptionsTemplate sets escapeHTML(false).

The 12 API templates disagree on which form they use for the same spec-prose slots:
- Operation parameter description and per-parameter example summary/description: escaped in node, dart, go, rust and swift; raw in java, kotlin, csharp (escapeXml), php, python, ruby and elixir.
- Tag description and tag/operation externalDocs description: escaped in node, go, rust and swift (dart escapes only the tag description); raw in the others.
- Operation-server variant description: escaped only in go.
- Model externalDocs description and model plural-example summary/description: escaped in all 12. csharp model.mustache:421/649 escapes twice (`{{summary}}` inside `lambda.escapeXml`), so `&` reaches the docs as a literal `&amp;` inside CDATA.

Result: a parameter described as `the pet's "nickname"` renders as `pet&#39;s \&quot;nickname\&quot;` in node/dart/go/rust/swift and as `pet's \"nickname\"` in the other 7. The named-entity part (`&quot;`, `&amp;`, `&lt;`) fails generatedCodeShouldNotContainHtmlEntities in those 5 languages only. This undoes AbstractBetterCodegen.preprocessOpenAPI, which decodes `&quot;` from buf/protoc specs precisely so it does not reach generated docs. The petstore golden is clean only because no parameter, tag or externalDocs prose contains `' " & < > = \``.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: None. The comment syntax is the same kind of prose slot in every language, and 7 languages already use triple braces there.

## F180 [medium] String default literals are escaped ad hoc per language: ruby/php keep stray backslashes, four SDKs break on an apostrophe, and python skips escapeText
- Status: **open** | Lens: L15-template-mechanics | Category: codegen | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: ruby, php, dart, node, python, kotlin

toDefaultValue for a string schema is written separately in each codegen:
- ruby, dart and php use `"'" + escapeText(default) + "'"`; node uses `getQuoteChar() + escapeText(...) + getQuoteChar()`.
- java, kotlin, go, rust, swift, csharp and elixir use `"\"" + escapeText(...) + "\""`.
- python uses `"'" + val.replace("'", "\\'") + "'"`, with no escapeText at all.

Because escapeText escapes `"` and `\` but not `'`, the results differ:
1. A default containing `'` is a syntax error in ruby, dart, php and node, but fine in python and the 7 double-quote languages.
2. A default containing `"` becomes `\"`. In ruby and php single-quoted strings that backslash is literal (verified: ruby `'a\"b'.length == 4`), so the in-memory default, and the serialized wire value, is `say \"hi\"` instead of `say "hi"`. node, dart and python decode it correctly.
3. python alone keeps raw newlines (syntax error) and undoubled backslashes (`\n` becomes a real newline), because it bypasses escapeText.
4. kotlin `"$USD"` and dart `'$USD'` interpolate.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: None.
- `src/main/java/io/github/mridang/codegen/generators/ruby/BetterRubyCodegen.java:750` — return "'" + escapeText(String.valueOf(resolved.getDefault())) + "'";
- `src/main/java/io/github/mridang/codegen/generators/php/BetterPHPCodegen.java:641` — .map(d -> "'" + escapeText(String.valueOf(d)) + "'")
- `src/main/java/io/github/mridang/codegen/generators/dart/BetterDartCodegen.java:581` — return "'" + escapeText(String.valueOf(resolved.getDefault())) + "'";
- `src/main/java/io/github/mridang/codegen/generators/node/BetterNodeCodegen.java:566` — return getQuoteChar() + escapeText(resolved.getDefault().toString()) + getQuoteChar();
- `src/main/java/io/github/mridang/codegen/generators/python/BetterPythonCodegen.java:768` — return "'" + val.replace("'", "\\'") + "'";
- `src/main/java/io/github/mridang/codegen/generators/kotlin/BetterKotlinCodegen.java:552` — return "\"" + escapeText(String.valueOf(unaliased.getDefault())) + "\"";

## F181 [medium] escapeUnsafeCharacters overrides do not match each language's real hazards: python's rule is dead, ruby's leaks '\#{' into comments, and elixir has no '#{' guard
- Status: **needs-spec** | Lens: L15-template-mechanics | Category: codegen | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: python, ruby, elixir

python: the override replaces `'''` because Python 'uses triple-quote docstrings', but every python template docstring is `"""` (api.mustache:52,102; model.mustache), and escapeText has already turned `"` into `\"`. The rule never protects anything; it only rewrites `'''` in prose to `'_'_'`.

ruby: the override rewrites `#{` to `\#{` (and `=begin`/`=end`) for every escapeText'd string. ruby renders those strings in `#` comments and single-quoted literals, where `#{` is inert, so `\#{` leaks into the docs. unescapeDocComment only reverses `\"` and `\\`.

elixir: it actually interpolates `#{...}` inside `"..."` and `"""` heredocs, and puts escapeText'd prose straight into `@moduledoc "{{{description}}}"` and `@doc """ {{{summary}}} {{{.}}} """`. Yet it inherits only the base `*/` rule. An operation description like `Fetches /users/#{id}` compiles in the other 11 SDKs but breaks elixir (undefined variable `id` under --warnings-as-errors) or silently interpolates.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: Each language does need its own rule, but the current rules target the wrong hazards: python's and ruby's are dead or harmful, and elixir's is missing.
- `src/main/java/io/github/mridang/codegen/generators/python/BetterPythonCodegen.java:748` — return input.replace("'''", "'_'_'");
- `src/main/resources/templates/python/api/api.mustache:52` —     """{{{description}}}"""
- `src/main/java/io/github/mridang/codegen/generators/ruby/BetterRubyCodegen.java:821` — return input.replace("=end", "=_end").replace("=begin", "=_begin").replace("#{", "\\#{");
- `src/main/resources/templates/elixir/api/api.mustache:23` —   @moduledoc "{{{description}}}"
- `src/main/resources/templates/elixir/api/api.mustache:99` —   @doc """\n  {{{summary}}}

## F190 [medium] Dart and Go spec setup rewrites the golden before the checks run, so the dart format gate cannot fail and go.mod/go.sum drift is hidden
- Status: **deferred** | Lens: L17-gates | Category: gate | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): False
- SDKs: dart, go

SharedRuntimeContainer runs getSetupCommands() inside /work and then snapshots the result (`cp -a /work /work-snapshot`, SharedRuntimeContainer.java:223). Every spec method restores that snapshot, not the committed golden. DartSpec's setup ends with `dart fix --apply ...` and then `dart format .`, so DartFormattingSpec's `dart format --set-exit-if-changed .` always runs on a tree that was formatted a moment earlier. It cannot fail, and formatting drift in the committed dart golden is never caught. GoSpec's setup runs `go mod tidy`, which rewrites go.mod/go.sum before GoBuildSpec, GoLintingSpec, GoClientSpec and GoWasmSpec, so an untidy manifest or a missing go.sum entry is hidden. A client's `make build` (`go build ./...`) has no tidy step and would hit that error. No other language's setup modifies sources or manifests; their setup only installs dependencies. This contradicts the AGENTS.md 'Known-thin gates' claim that every check runs 'in check mode ... no write-mode-posing-as-check'. The DartSpec setup comment is also stale: it says '770 info-level findings remain ... they don't fail the spec', but DartLintingSpec runs `dart analyze --fatal-warnings --fatal-infos`. The setup's `dart fix` codes (always_use_package_imports, directives_ordering, document_ignores) are not enabled by `include: package:lints/recommended.yaml`, so that step does nothing.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: None. The generator already runs dart format and go mod tidy at generation time, so the golden should pass without these setup steps; the checks should run on the committed tree.

## F192 [medium] Five SDKs' decompression integration tests call a public internet host and pass whether or not the body was encoded
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L17-gates | Category: test-gap | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: ruby, python, node, go, dart

java, kotlin, csharp, php, rust and elixir run their 'decompresses gzip/brotli/zstd response' integration tests against the chasm fixture's `/test/compressed/<enc>` endpoints. The fixture's `x-chasm-content-encoding` makes it really send that encoding, so asserting on the body proves the client decoded it. ruby, python, node, go and dart send the same three tests to `https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1` and assert only status 200 and that the body contains 'userId'. Nothing makes that server use the requested encoding: an identity response passes, so the tests do not show that the br/zstd/gzip decode path ran. The tests also depend on the public internet and a third-party host (node's own comment adds a 30s timeout 'because jsonplaceholder.typicode.com is an external host'), so CI can be flaky or blocked offline. The chasm endpoints are already in every SDK's fixture openapi.yaml.

(2) csharp: CSharpStaticAnalysisSpec builds PetstoreClient.Test.csproj with `--warnaserror`, but that project sets none of AnalysisLevel=latest-all, AnalysisMode=All or EnforceCodeStyleInBuild (the SDK csproj sets all three). The test code is therefore checked only against the default analyzer set, while the SDK gets every CA rule. (3) java: spotbugs-maven-plugin defaults to includeTests=false and the pom does not override it, so SpotBugs never sees src/test, though checkstyle sets includeTestSourceDirectory=true. (elixir's `mix test` also runs without --warnings-as-errors. The ElixirClientSpec comment gives a reason: deprecation warnings at call sites cannot be suppressed in elixir. That is borderline-forced and not recorded in AGENTS.md.)

Reviewer suspected this is forced: None for swift, csharp or java. elixir's test exemption is borderline (no per-call deprecation suppression).

(go, python, ruby and elixir are fairly exempt: `#` is their only comment syntax, or `//` is the godoc doc-comment syntax.)

Reviewer suspected this is forced: None for kotlin or rust, which both separate doc comments from line comments. csharp's Models exclusion has no stated reason.

- Status: **partial** (done in csharp, php, swift; still open for go) | Lens: L18a-wire-request | Category: wire | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: php, swift, go, csharp

Most SDKs write `/` and non-ASCII characters as-is in JSON request bodies (verified: java, kotlin, python, ruby, node, dart, rust, elixir). php calls `json_encode($sanitized, $flags)` with flags 0, so it sends every `/` as `\/` and every non-ASCII character as `\uXXXX`: Pet{name:"café", photoUrls:["https://x/y.png"]} becomes `"café"` and `"https:\/\/x\/y.png"`. swift's JSONEncoder and JSONSerialization are configured without `.withoutEscapingSlashes`, so every photoUrls value and every base64 `format: byte` value containing `/` goes out as `\/` (confirmed with swift on macOS: `{"name":"café\/ü","photoUrls":["https:\/\/x\/y.png"]}`). swift's own test locks this in (ObjectSerializerTests.swift:985-989). Two smaller cases: go's encoding/json always escapes U+2028 and U+2029, even with SetEscapeHTML(false). csharp's `JavaScriptEncoder.UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping` still writes characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane (emoji) as `😀` pairs, based on known .NET behaviour (I could not run .NET here). Every body-carrying operation is affected (addPet, updatePet, placeOrder, setPetAvatarThumbnail, …). AGENTS records that go's HTML-escaping was turned off so bytes go out literally "like every other SDK"; php and swift break that same rule. Fix: php `JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE`; swift `outputFormatting = .withoutEscapingSlashes` and `options: .withoutEscapingSlashes`.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: php/swift: none (flags exist). go U+2028/2029 and csharp supplementary-plane escaping are stdlib behaviours that would need a custom writer; borderline

- `src/main/resources/templates/php/object_serializer.mustache:268` — $json = json_encode($sanitized, $flags);
- `src/spec/resources/generated/swift/Sources/PetstoreClient/ObjectSerializer.swift:83` — let encoder = JSONEncoder()

- `src/main/resources/templates/swift/object_serializer.mustache:77` — let encoder = JSONEncoder()

## F199 [medium] Query-value encoding differs in 2 languages: java escapes ~ but not *; node keeps ! * ' ( ) ~ literal
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L18a-wire-request | Category: wire | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: java, node

Nine SDKs encode non-allowReserved query keys and values with the RFC 3986 unreserved set `A-Za-z0-9-._~`: csharp, php, python, ruby, dart, go, rust, swift, elixir. Kotlin is broken separately (previous finding). Two others differ on the same input. java uses `URLEncoder.encode(...).replace("+","%20")`, which escapes `~` as %7E and keeps `*` literal. node uses `encodeURIComponent`, which keeps `! * ' ( ) ~` literal; fetch's WHATWG URL parser then escapes `'` back to %27. For getPetByName(category="a~b*c!d'e(f)g"), confirmed against runtime encoders: python/elixir/ruby send `a~b%2Ac%21d%27e%28f%29g`, java sends `a%7Eb*c%21d%27e%28f%29g`, node sends `a~b*c!d%27e(f)g`. java already restores `%7E`→`~` in its path and allowReserved encoders (ValueSerializer.java:123, :183). PetApiTest.java:533-544 asserts that `~` must never become %7E, but only on the path. The plain query encoder was never aligned. node's own path encoder (value-serializer.ts:211-224) shows the intended canonical set. This is not covered by the R8-10 OAuth note, which is about the token, Basic and authorize paths only.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: none; java already post-processes URLEncoder output elsewhere, and node already post-processes encodeURIComponent in encodePathSegment

## F200 [medium] dart: a multipart array of strings sends only its last element
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L18a-wire-request | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: dart

dart's multipart builder handles a non-binary List field by calling `_addMultipartField` once per element. For a String element that runs `request.fields[name] = value`, and `http.MultipartRequest.fields` is a Map, so each element overwrites the previous one and only the last survives. The code comment says the list "expands into one part per element (repeated keys, as for the urlencoded form)", which is what java (DefaultApiClient.java:888), python (default_api_client.py:868), node, go, rust, swift, ruby, php, csharp, kotlin and elixir actually do. The same happens for num/bool elements (`request.fields[name] = value.toString()`). This is latent in the petstore, which has no multipart string array (`files` is binary and goes through `request.files.add`), but any spec with a multipart array of scalars loses data silently.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: none; package:http supports repeated text parts via request.files.add(MultipartFile.fromString(...)) or a custom body
- `src/spec/resources/generated/dart/lib/src/abstract_api_client.dart:212` — /* A non-binary array form field expands into one part per element

- `src/main/resources/templates/dart/abstract_api_client.mustache:505` — request.fields[name] = value;
- `src/spec/resources/generated/java/src/main/java/com/example/petstore/DefaultApiClient.java:888` — addMultipartField(byteArrays, boundary, fieldName, item);

## F201 [medium] ruby: Faraday decodes and re-encodes the query string, which undoes allowReserved, sorts parameters and drops repeated keys
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L18a-wire-request | Category: wire | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: ruby

Ruby builds the query string itself in base_api.rb `build_query_string`, then passes the full URL to `Faraday::Connection#run_request`. Faraday's `Request#url` parses that query with the connection's params_encoder (`QueryParamsEncoder.decode` → `NestedParamsEncoder.decode`), and `build_exclusive_url` re-encodes it with `NestedParamsEncoder.encode` plus `Utils.escape` (ESCAPE_RE `/[^a-zA-Z0-9 .~_-]/`). I ran the installed faraday-2.14.2 encoder on a query matching the golden output. (1) allowReserved is undone: `revision=v1.0/beta:rc1` goes out as `revision=v1.0%2Fbeta%3Arc1`, while all other SDKs send `/` and `:` literally (the petstore's own documented example). (2) Every query is reordered alphabetically (`@sort_params = true`), and deepObject sub-keys are sorted as well. (3) Repeated keys collapse to the last value (`m=1&m=2` → `m=2`), so any exploded array query parameter (OAS default style form, explode true) loses all but its last element. The petstore has no exploded query array, so (3) is latent. Ruby's only allowReserved test is the unit test of `encode_query_allowing_reserved` (value_serializer_test.rb:477); no ruby test checks the URL that Faraday actually sends. The QueryParamsEncoder was added only to turn `+` back into %20, and its comment wrongly says it leaves every other character as Faraday encodes it. Fix: pass params separately, or give the encoder an identity decode/encode that keeps the pre-built query unchanged.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: none; Faraday accepts a custom params_encoder whose decode/encode can pass the query through unchanged
- `src/spec/resources/generated/ruby/lib/petstore/client/default_api_client.rb:65` — module QueryParamsEncoder
- `src/spec/resources/generated/ruby/lib/petstore/client/default_api_client.rb:67` — ::Faraday::NestedParamsEncoder.encode(params)&.gsub('+', '%20')
- `src/spec/resources/generated/ruby/lib/petstore/client/default_api_client.rb:453` — f.options.params_encoder = QueryParamsEncoder
- `src/main/resources/templates/ruby/default_api_client.mustache:60` — module QueryParamsEncoder
- `src/spec/resources/generated/ruby/lib/petstore/client/api/base_api.rb:242` — ::Petstore::Client::ValueSerializer.encode_query_allowing_reserved(str)
- `src/spec/resources/generated/ruby/test/value_serializer_test.rb:477` — _(Petstore::Client::ValueSerializer.encode_query_allowing_reserved('v1.0/beta:rc1')).must_equal('v1.0/beta:rc1')

## F202 [medium] AGENTS claims node and python preserve full decimal precision for `type: number`, but both decode weightKg through a binary float; both also accept a quoted string
- Status: **open** (documents corrected; the code or template part is still open) | Lens: L18b-wire-response | Category: doc-truth | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: node, python

AGENTS.md:246 lists node ('branded Decimal + JSON.rawJSON') and python ('Decimal') among the FIVE precision-preserving SDKs. That holds only on encode. On decode, node's parseJson is a plain JSON.parse, and the constructor then does `String(this.weightKg)`. I checked: 12.34567890123456789 becomes "12.345678901234567", 1.0 becomes "1", and 1e400 becomes "Infinity". python's parse_json is json.loads with the default parse_float=float, so pydantic receives a float. I checked: Decimal('12.345678901234567'). java, kotlin and csharp read the number text exactly (I checked java: 12.34567890123456789). Wire acceptance also diverges: `"weightKg":"1.5"` (quoted) is rejected by java (I checked), kotlin, csharp and the 7 native-float SDKs. python's lax Decimal accepts it, and node accepts ANY string ("abc", "NaN") as the branded Decimal. node's README 'Decimal / format: number precision' section talks only about int64 and never mentions this loss. Fixes: JSON.parse with a reviver using context.source (available in the same runtime that has JSON.rawJSON) and `json.loads(parse_float=Decimal)` or pydantic's lossless JSON path. Otherwise correct AGENTS.

## F204 [medium] Fractional/float literal for an integer field: java silently truncates (7.5->7), node keeps 1.5, swift accepts 7.0/1e2; the rest reject
- Status: **partial** (done in java, node; still open for swift) | Lens: L18b-wire-response | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True

Case: Order/Pet `id` (int64) or `quantity` (int32) carrying 1.5, 7.0 or 1e2. java: Jackson's ACCEPT_FLOAT_AS_INT is enabled by default and ALLOW_COERCION_OF_SCALARS does not override it. I checked: `{"quantity":7.5}` gives 7, `{"id":1.5}` gives 1, `{"quantity":1e2}` gives 100, and getInventory `{"a":7.5}` gives {a=7]. ## F206 [medium] Null element in a top-level model array (findPetsByStatus [null, {...}]) splits three ways: kept, rejected, or silently dropped

The Pet items schema is non-nullable. For `[null,{"name":"a","photoUrls":[]}]` the SDKs disagree. KEEP the null: java (I checked: `[null, P]`), csharp List<Pet>, ruby (convert_to_type(nil) gives nil), elixir and php (deserializeInternal(null) gives null). DROP silently: node, whose deserializeArray filters nulls for model element types, so the caller gets a shorter array with shifted indices. Only one of these can be the contract. Rejecting matches the schema.

## F207 [medium] go matches JSON keys case-insensitively: {"ID":7} sets Pet.Id, and {"name":"Rex","NAME":"Evil"} yields Name="Evil"
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L18b-wire-response | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: go

go decodes models via `json.Unmarshal(data, aux)` (encoding/json v1). v1 falls back to a case-insensitive field match when no exact key matches. A response key that differs only in case from a declared property is therefore bound to that field. `{"name":"Rex","photoUrls":[],"ID":7}` gives Id=7 in go, while the other 11 ignore the unknown key and leave id null. With `"name":"Rex","NAME":"Evil"`, go's later case-folded key overwrites, giving Name="Evil" vs "Rex" everywhere else. The Gap AJ required check uses the exact-case raw map, so the presence check and the decoded value can disagree. This is not forced: UnmarshalJSON already builds the raw map and can reject or ignore non-exact keys, or use json/v2 case-sensitive matching.

## F208 [medium] java coerces a JSON number/boolean into a String field ({"name":42} -> "42"); the other 11 reject
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L18b-wire-response | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: java

Jackson's ALLOW_COERCION_OF_SCALARS=false covers only number, boolean and date targets. String (LogicalType.Textual) is excluded, so int->String, float->String and boolean->String coercion stays on. I checked this against jackson-databind 2.19.4 (the golden's version) with the golden mapper config: `{"name":42}` decodes to name="42" and `{"name":true}` to "true". kotlin rejects this and has explicit tests for it (unquotedNumberScalarOnStringFieldThrows). csharp (STJ), go, rust, swift (I checked: typeMismatch), python StrictStr, dart `as String`, php assertPrimitiveTypes, ruby/elixir strict 'String' clauses and node's typeof check all reject it. The java comment claims parity ('Matches the other SDKs, which reject wrong-typed primitives'), but its tests cover only the String->number and number->boolean directions. Fix: `coercionConfigFor(LogicalType.Textual).setCoercion(CoercionInputShape.Integer|Float|Boolean, CoercionAction.Fail)`, plus a test.

- `src/main/resources/templates/java/object_serializer.mustache:393` — .configure(MapperFeature.ALLOW_COERCION_OF_SCALARS, false)
- `src/spec/resources/generated/kotlin/src/test/kotlin/com/example/petstore/ObjectSerializerTest.kt:443` — fun unquotedNumberScalarOnStringFieldThrows()

- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L18b-wire-response | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: python

Every model sets `ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True)` and responses decode via `klass.model_validate(data)`, so pydantic accepts BOTH the alias and the field name. I checked with pydantic 2.12 on a reproduction of the generated Pet: `{"name":"x","photo_urls":["a"]}` decodes successfully with photo_urls={'a'}. The other 11 reject it as missing the required `photoUrls`. Likewise `{"pet_id":5}` on Order populates pet_id in python, while the other 11 ignore the unknown key and leave it null. The template comment justifies populate_by_name for constructors only; pydantic >=2.11 can keep that (validate_by_name) while decoding responses with model_validate(..., by_alias=True, by_name=False).

## F212 [medium] ruby/elixir silently turn a non-object nested model into nil (and elixir passes wrong-kind Set/map fields through raw)
- Status: **fixed** (done in ruby; still open for elixir) | Lens: L18b-wire-response | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: ruby, elixir

`{"name":"x","photoUrls":[],"category":"oops"}` (or 5, or [1,2]): ruby's deserialize_model does `return nil unless data.is_a?(Hash)` and elixir's `deserialize_model(_data, _module), do: nil`, so category becomes nil and the payload is accepted. java, kotlin, csharp, go, rust, swift, python and dart reject it with a SerializationError. In elixir, the `MapSet.t(`/`%{String.t() =>` container clauses are guarded by is_list/is_map and have no raising fallback (unlike the `[` clause). So `"photoUrls":"abc"` falls through to the model-name fallback `true -> data`, and Pet.photo_urls holds the raw string "abc". For a TOP-LEVEL non-object body (e.g. getPetById returns `[]` or `"x"`), both SDKs produce data=nil: the WithHttpInfo variant returns a nil body silently, and the convenience method raises ApiError 'Expected a response body ... but received none'. The other SDKs raise SerializationError, so this is also an error-type divergence.

- `src/main/resources/templates/ruby/object_serializer.mustache:456` — return nil unless data.is_a?(Hash)
- `src/spec/resources/generated/elixir/lib/petstore_client/object_serializer.ex:1033` — defp deserialize_model(_data, _module), do: nil
- `src/spec/resources/generated/elixir/lib/petstore_client/object_serializer.ex:670` — def convert_to_type(data, "MapSet.t(" <> rest) when is_list(data) do
- `src/main/resources/templates/elixir/object_serializer.mustache:998` — defp deserialize_model(_data, _module), do: nil

## F213 [medium] Integer formats: int32 overflow and fractional numbers are accepted by 6 SDKs and rejected by 6; java silently truncates 1.5 to 1; node keeps 1.5 and rounds int64 above 2^53. No boundary test

Behaviour on decode: `3000000000` into int32 is rejected by java/kotlin/csharp/go/rust/swift. python (StrictInt is unbounded), ruby (`is_a?(Integer)`), node (`typeof === 'number'`), php (64-bit int), dart (64-bit int) and elixir (`is_integer`) accept it and later re-send a value the schema forbids. `1.5` into int32/int64: java truncates SILENTLY to 1 (Jackson ACCEPT_FLOAT_AS_INT stays at its default; ALLOW_COERCION_OF_SCALARS=false does not cover float-to-int; checked against jackson-databind 2.21.1). node accepts 1.5 unchanged. python/ruby/kotlin/go/rust/swift/csharp reject it. int64 `9007199254740993` is silently rounded by node's `number`. Proposed fixture: a probe op `/probe.v1.RELAYService/Counters` returning `{type: object, properties: {small: {type: integer, format: int32}, big: {type: integer, format: int64}}}`. Add per-SDK unit tests decoding `{"small":3000000000}`, `{"small":1.5}` and `{"big":9007199254740993}`, with one agreed outcome (reject as SerializationError).

## F214 [medium] Non-string scalar multipart parts (boolean, date-time, date, $ref enum, uuid) are encoded differently in every SDK. Petstore's multipart scalars are all plain strings
- Status: **fixed** (done via decision D36 in all SDKs (batches 5-6, branch parity/spec-expansion)) | Lens: L19-spec-coverage | Category: spec-coverage | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: java, kotlin, python, ruby, go, csharp, php, node, dart, rust, swift, elixir

The only scalar multipart fields in petstore are `documentType` (an inline enum that every SDK types as String) and `notes`, so the scalar-part encoders are only ever given strings. The encoders differ. java's addMultipartField sends String/Number/Boolean as text but anything else (OffsetDateTime, LocalDate, an enum, UUID) as a JSON part with `Content-Type: application/json`, so a date-time becomes the quoted `"2024-01-15T10:30:00.000+00:00"`. kotlin does the same (default_api_client 462-471). python's fallback is `f'{value}'`: a bool is `True`, a datetime is `2024-01-15 10:30:00+00:00` (space, no millis), and a `(str, Enum)` member formats as `Cls.MEMBER` on Python >= 3.11 (pyproject requires >= 3.13). go uses `fmt.Sprintf("%v", v)`, which prints the Go struct form for its DateTime type. ruby interpolates `#{value}`, so a Time becomes `2024-01-15 10:30:00 UTC`. Only the form-urlencoded path uses each SDK's canonical `stringify`. Proposed YAML: extend uploadPetDocument's multipart schema with `isPrimary: {type: boolean}`, `takenAt: {type: string, format: date-time}`, `swatch: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Swatch'}`, `pages: {type: integer, format: int32}`. Assert each part's body and headers byte-for-byte (`true`, `2024-01-15T10:30:00.000+00:00`, `red`, no part Content-Type).

Reviewer suspected this is forced: none

- `src/main/resources/templates/python/default_api_client.mustache:971` — part = f'--{boundary}\r\nContent-Disposition: {disposition}\r\n\r\n{value}\r\n'
- `src/main/resources/templates/go/base_api.mustache:486` — return writer.WriteField(name, fmt.Sprintf("%v", v))
- `src/main/resources/templates/ruby/default_api_client.mustache:571` — "--#{boundary}\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name=\"#{safe_name}\"\r\n\r\n#{value}\r\n"
- `src/main/resources/templates/kotlin/default_api_client.mustache:462` — is String, is Number, is Boolean -> append(fieldName, value.toString())

## F215 [medium] Required + nullable properties: node/elixir accept an explicit null, kotlin/rust/swift/python/dart reject it, go silently zero-values it, java accepts it; all 12 drop the key when serializing a null. Not exercised
- Status: **open** | Lens: L19-spec-coverage | Category: spec-coverage | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: node, elixir, kotlin, rust, swift, python, dart, go, java, csharp, php, ruby

The only nullable property in petstore (Defaults.label, `type: [string, "null"]`) is optional. For a property that is both `required` and nullable, the templates diverge. node's constructor check accepts `null` and rejects only `undefined` (node model 533-542). elixir leaves nullable requireds out of required_fields (elixir model 399-401). kotlin types every required var non-null (`{{^required}}?{{/required}}`), so kotlinx rejects `null`. rust (`T`, not `Option<T>`), swift (non-optional let), python (`name: {{dataType}}`, not Optional) and dart (`as String`) also reject. go types every required var as a non-pointer with no omitempty (go model 152-153): a decoded null silently becomes ""/0 and is re-sent as ""/0, not null. java accepts null. On the serialize side every SDK's null-omission policy (Jackson NON_NULL, STJ WhenWritingNull, `exclude_none`, SKIP_NULL_VALUES, encodeIfPresent, skip_serializing_if) DROPS a required key whose value is null, which violates `required`. Proposed YAML: add to Defaults `required: [note]` and `note: {type: [string, "null"]}`. Test decoding `{"note":null}` and serializing a model with note=null; the expected bytes are `{"note":null}`.

## F216 [medium] form-urlencoded bodies: ruby skips ObjectSerializer.stringify and nested objects fall back to each language's own string repr. Masked because petstore's form fields are only string/array-of-string/date
- Status: **fixed** (done via decision D39 in all SDKs (batches 5-6, branch parity/spec-expansion)) | Lens: L19-spec-coverage | Category: spec-coverage | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: ruby, java, kotlin, python, node, go, csharp, php, dart, rust, swift, elixir

setPetPreferences is the only x-www-form-urlencoded op. Its fields (nickname, tags, note, renewalDate) are all strings or a Date, and ruby's `Date#to_s` happens to equal the canonical form. (1) ruby's serialize_body is `URI.encode_www_form(body.compact)`: Ruby `to_s` on each value, never `ObjectSerializer.stringify`. A date-time field therefore goes out as `t=2024-01-15+10%3A30%3A00+UTC` (checked locally) where every other SDK sends canonical RFC 3339. A duration goes out as `PT1H` instead of `3600s`. A nil element inside an array emits an empty/stray `tags` token where java/kotlin/python/node/go/elixir skip it. (2) A nested object or map field (OAS form style / deepObject encoding) reaches each SDK's generic stringify fallback: java/kotlin `toString()` (`Pet{...}` / `Pet(...)`), python `str()` (pydantic repr), node `String(value)` = `[object Object]`, go `fmt.Sprintf("%v")`, ruby `to_s`. Twelve different byte strings. Proposed YAML: add to setPetPreferences' form schema `remindAt: {type: string, format: date-time}`, `snooze: {type: string, format: duration}`, `location: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/PhotoMetadataLocation'}`, with `encoding: {location: {style: deepObject, explode: true}}`. Assert `remindAt=2024-01-15T10%3A30%3A00.000%2B00%3A00`, `snooze=3600s` and `location%5Blat%5D=1.5`.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: none

- `src/main/resources/templates/elixir/base_api.mustache:427` — URI.encode_www_form({{moduleName}}.ObjectSerializer.stringify(val))
- `src/main/resources/templates/node/object_serializer.mustache:729` — return String(value);
- `src/main/resources/templates/go/object_serializer.mustache:44` — return fmt.Sprintf("%v", v)
- `src/main/resources/templates/python/object_serializer.mustache:561` — return str(value)

## F217 [medium] format: uuid: swift sends UPPERCASE UUIDs, 8 SDKs lowercase, ruby/elixir/node send the caller's string verbatim; petstore has no uuid field
- Status: **open** | Lens: L19-spec-coverage | Category: spec-coverage | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: swift, ruby, elixir, node, java, kotlin, csharp, php, python, dart, go, rust

Neither spec declares `format: uuid`. swift maps it to Foundation.UUID and its ObjectSerializer has no UUID handling, so JSONEncoder uses `uuidString`, which is uppercase. Checked locally: encoding `UUID(uuidString: "e621e1f8-...")` gives `{"id":"E621E1F8-C36C-495A-93FC-0C247A3E6E5F"}`, and query/path stringification uses the same description. java UUID, kotlin Uuid, csharp Guid, python uuid.UUID, go uuid.UUID, rust uuid::Uuid, php Symfony Uid (toRfc4122) and dart's UuidValue (`source.toLowerCase()`) all emit lowercase. ruby and elixir type it as String and validate only on DECODE: validate_uuid returns the value unchanged, and nothing validates on encode, so a caller's mixed-case or malformed value goes out verbatim. node's branded `UUID` string likewise passes the caller's casing through. Proposed YAML: add to Order `trackingId: {type: string, format: uuid}` and a path param `/store/order/by-tracking/{trackingId}` (format: uuid). Assert lowercase canonical bytes on the wire in all 12, and that a malformed value is rejected before dispatch.

## F221 [medium] The forced-divergence note says python and node preserve full decimal precision; both lose it on decode
- Status: **fixed** (AGENTS.md / PARITY_TODO.md corrected against the code (round 9 doc pass)) | Lens: L20-doc-truth | Category: doc-truth | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: python, node

AGENTS says five SDKs 'preserve full textual precision' for bare `type: number`, naming python (Decimal) and node (branded Decimal + JSON.rawJSON), against seven lossy native-float SDKs. Python parses with plain `json.loads`, with no `parse_float=Decimal`, so the value is an IEEE double before pydantic turns it into a Decimal. JsonNumber's PlainSerializer then converts back through `float(value)` on encode, so python is lossy in both directions; its own README admits the encode loss. Node decodes with plain `JSON.parse`, and the model then does `String(this.weightKg)` on the already-rounded number, so only the encode path (JSON.rawJSON) keeps the text. Only java, kotlin and csharp read the number's source text, so the 'five' are really three plus two that are lossy on decode.
- `src/spec/resources/generated/python/petstore_client/object_serializer.py:220` — return json.loads(json_string, parse_constant=ObjectSerializer._reject_nonfinite_constant,)
- `src/spec/resources/generated/python/petstore_client/_types.py:87` — JsonNumber = Annotated[Decimal, PlainSerializer(lambda value: float(value), return_type=float, when_used="json")]
- `src/spec/resources/generated/node/src/object-serializer.ts:274` — return JSON.parse(json);
- `src/spec/resources/generated/node/src/models/pet.ts:161` — if (this.weightKg != null && typeof this.weightKg === "number") { this.weightKg = String(this.weightKg) as unknown as Decimal;
- `AGENTS.md:246` — FIVE preserve full textual precision — java/kotlin (BigDecimal), csharp (decimal), python (Decimal), node (branded Decimal + JSON.rawJSON)

AGENTS.md (Forced divergences) says five SDKs "preserve full textual precision", including python (Decimal) and node (branded Decimal + JSON.rawJSON). The code contradicts this.
- python, decode: ObjectSerializer parses with `json.loads(json_string, parse_constant=...)` and no `parse_float=Decimal`, so the number is already a binary float before pydantic coerces it to Decimal.
- python, encode: the `JsonNumber` alias serializes with `PlainSerializer(lambda value: float(value), when_used="json")`, which narrows to float.
- Verified with pydantic 2.12: `{"w":12.34567890123456789}` decodes to `Decimal('12.345678901234567')`, and `Decimal("12.34567890123456789")` encodes as `12.345678901234567`.
- node, decode: `ObjectSerializer.parseJson` is plain `JSON.parse(json)`, then the model coerces with `String(this.weightKg)`. Verified: `12.345678901234567890` becomes "12.345678901234567" and `12345678901234567890` becomes "12345678901234567000". Only encode is lossless (JSON.rawJSON).

node's README caveat covers int64 only, not Decimal. java, kotlin and csharp really do round-trip losslessly, so the precision-preserving group is three languages, not five. Node can decode losslessly with the reviver `context.source` from the same json-parse-with-source proposal it already relies on for rawJSON. Python can pass `parse_float=Decimal` and emit the raw decimal text. Otherwise AGENTS should list python and node with the lossy group, and their READMEs should carry the caveat.

- `src/spec/resources/generated/node/README.md:62` — ### Decimal / `format: number` precision (only discusses int64)

## F225 [medium] Configuration and TransportOptions print secrets (proxy password, Authorization default header) in 7 SDKs; every authenticator redacts
- Status: **open** | Lens: L21-api-surface | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: python, rust, ruby, elixir, node, php, go

The SDK has a redaction policy: every authenticator in all 12 masks its secret in toString, repr, Debug or inspect as `***`. The same secrets also sit in two other public value types. First, the proxy URL holds `user:pass@` credentials by design (python, dart and elixir parse the userinfo into Proxy-Authorization, java pre-computes it, and python's comment says this matches the other 11). Second, the default headers of Configuration and TransportOptions hold credentials: the generated docs use `.defaultHeader("Authorization", "Bearer token")` as the example, and java's PetApiTest does exactly that. Those values print in plain text in 7 languages:
- python: the frozen-dataclass repr prints `proxy='http://user:pass@h'` and the default_headers mapping (verified in /tmp).
- rust: `#[derive(Debug)]` on both structs prints proxy and default_headers; TransportOptions also prints the CA PEM bytes.
- ruby: the default `inspect` dumps the instance variables.
- elixir: the struct `inspect` dumps them, although authenticators use `@derive {Inspect, except: [:token]}`.
- node: `util.inspect` and `console.log` dump the readonly fields, although authenticators define `[nodejs.util.inspect.custom]`.
- php: var_dump and print_r dump the readonly props, although authenticators define `__debugInfo`.
- go: `%+v` prints the defaultHeaders map contents. The proxy is a *url.URL, so only its address prints.
In java, kotlin, csharp, dart and swift the classes have no field-dumping representation (Object, Instance-of, or type-name default), so nothing leaks. Same object, same secret, different logging exposure: either redact (mask proxy userinfo and sensitive header values) in all 12, or never dump in all 12.

## F226 [medium] TransportOptions has a public constructor that skips the builder's proxy validation in php, python, ruby and node
- Status: **fixed** (done in node, php; still open for python, ruby) | Lens: L21-api-surface | Category: api-shape | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: php, python, ruby, node

PARITY_TODO T2-10 says TransportOptions is builder-only "because it has validated invariants": the builder rejects a proxy URL that has no host or does not use http or https. That holds in java (package-private ctor), kotlin (private constructor), csharp (internal ctor), dart (TransportOptions._), swift (fileprivate init), go (unexported fields, Build() returns an error) and rust (private fields, build() returns Result). In php, python, ruby and node the value type has a public constructor that does no checking at all, so the invariant can be skipped. Examples: `new TransportOptions(proxy: 'socks5://h:1080')` (php), `TransportOptions(proxy='ftp://x')` (python, since __post_init__ only wraps the headers), `TransportOptions.new(proxy: 'ftp://x', ...)` (ruby), `new TransportOptions({proxy: 'ftp://x', ...})` (node). Each is accepted, and the bad URL goes straight to Guzzle, urllib3, Faraday or undici. Those libraries then throw their own exceptions or misroute traffic, against the error contract, which says a caller mistake raises the language's built-in error. The same input is rejected up front in the other languages. None of these is forced: php and node can declare a private constructor, ruby can use `private_class_method :new`, and python's frozen dataclass can run the same proxy check in __post_init__. Elixir's `%TransportOptions{}` struct literal is the one forced bypass, since struct literals are always public.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: Python has no private constructors, but __post_init__ can validate, so it is not forced. php, ruby and node all have constructor-hiding features.

## F227 [medium] java, node and rust let callers build a model that is missing required properties; the other 8 non-go SDKs reject it

Pet's required `name` and `photoUrls` cannot be left out at construction in kotlin (non-default vals), csharp (`required` members), php (required ctor args), python (pydantic ValidationError), ruby (Dry::Struct raises), dart (`required` named params), swift (memberwise init) or elixir (`@enforce_keys`). Go's zero-value struct is the forced exception.
- java: a public no-arg `Pet()` leaves `name` null. All fields are public and non-final, so `pet.name = null` also works after construction. With NON_NULL inclusion the request is sent without `name`, and no client-side error is raised.

But the `@JsonCreator` constructor already handles deserialization, so the public ctor only serves tests (PetApiTest does `new Pet(); pet.id = ...`). These are public construction paths that accept input the other SDKs reject before dispatch.

## F228 [medium] Cancellation is impossible in go, csharp and node, which accept no context.Context, CancellationToken or AbortSignal; python's asyncio cancellation leaves the request running. AGENTS' C# cancellation claim is unreachable
- Status: **open** | Lens: L22-lifecycle | Category: api-shape | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: go, csharp, node, python, dart, java, kotlin, swift, rust, elixir

AGENTS: 'Never rewrap the platform's cancellation ... a cancelled C# request as OperationCanceledException'. In java (Thread.interrupt), kotlin (Job.cancel), swift (Task.cancel), rust (dropping the future) and elixir (killing the process), a caller can abort an in-flight request with the platform's own mechanism. go builds every request with context.Background() and no operation takes a ctx, so a go caller cannot cancel. Every csharp ...Async operation and SendRequestAsync lacks the idiomatic CancellationToken parameter, so a csharp caller cannot cancel. The only test reaches OperationCanceledException through the internal DefaultApiClient(HttpClient) seam plus CancelPendingRequests. node's fetch gets only AbortSignal.timeout and the operations take no signal. python's operations are async def but run the sync urllib3 call through asyncio.to_thread. Cancelling the asyncio task raises CancelledError while the worker thread carries the HTTP request (a POST, say) through to completion. dart Futures are not cancellable and no abort hook is exposed. Cancellation tests exist only for java, kotlin, swift and csharp (internal seam).

Reviewer suspected this is forced: AGENTS 'The SDK has no cancellation API of its own'. But context.Context, CancellationToken and AbortSignal are the platform's cancellation primitives, not SDK-specific ones.

## F229 [medium] Connection reuse differs: ruby never keeps a connection alive, python's pool holds one connection per host under its concurrent async facade, and go uses a zero-value http.Transport
- Status: **partial** (done in go, python; still open for ruby) | Lens: L22-lifecycle | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): False
- SDKs: ruby, python, go

ruby: build_connection uses Faraday's default net_http adapter, which creates a new Net::HTTP per request and wraps it in http.start {...} (faraday-net_http 3.4.x net_http.rb: Net::HTTP.new at :54/:59, http.start at :112). Every ruby request therefore pays a fresh TCP and TLS handshake. The comment claiming the cached connection preserves 'the underlying socket pool / keepalive' is false, and close() has nothing to release. python: urllib3.PoolManager(**kwargs) uses the default maxsize=1 per host, while the async facade runs requests concurrently through asyncio.to_thread. Every concurrent request beyond the first opens a new connection and has it discarded on return, with a 'Connection pool is full' warning. go: buildHTTPClient starts from &http.Transport{} instead of http.DefaultTransport.Clone(). That gives no IdleConnTimeout (idle sockets are held until the server closes them), MaxIdleConnsPerHost=2, no dial or TLS-handshake timeout or TCP keep-alive, and no ProxyFromEnvironment. java, kotlin, csharp, node, rust, swift, php, dart and elixir use pooled keep-alive clients with library-default limits.

- `src/spec/resources/generated/python/petstore_client/default_api_client.py:312` — self._pool_manager = urllib3.PoolManager(**kwargs)
- `src/spec/resources/generated/go/pkg/default_api_client.go:272` — transport := &http.Transport{}
- `src/main/resources/templates/go/default_api_client.mustache:265` — transport := &http.Transport{}

## F230 [medium] OIDC rediscovery after the Cache-Control max-age expires throws away the exchanged authorization-code tokens (all 12); discovery is single-flight only in java/go

- SDKs: java, kotlin, csharp, php, python, ruby, node, dart, go, rust, swift, elixir

When discoveryExpiry passes (86400 s by default, or whatever max-age the OP sends; max-age=0 makes it immediate), every SDK builds a brand-new OAuth2AuthorizationCodeAuthenticator with tokenExchanged=false and a fresh token manager. The access and refresh tokens from exchangeCode are discarded, and the next getAuthHeaders throws 'Must call exchangeCode() before making API requests' (or its equivalent), which cannot be recovered without a new user authorization. Refreshing the endpoints should carry the token state over. Separately, discovery is serialized only in java (synchronized getDelegate) and go (mutex held across fetch). kotlin/csharp/swift/python/ruby/node/dart/php/elixir fetch outside any lock: concurrent callers fire duplicate discovery requests, and the last writer replaces the delegate, which can silently discard a delegate that exchangeCode just populated. rust instead fails the concurrent caller (separate finding).

## F232 [medium] csharp and dart silently drop a multipart body when replaying it on a 307/308 redirect

On 307/308 the original method and body must be replayed. csharp rebuilds the follow-up only for byte[] and string bodies, and throws for Stream. A multipart body (Dictionary<string, object>) matches no branch, so next.Content stays null and the redirected POST goes out with no body. dart likewise copies only Uint8List or String into the follow-up http.Request. ## F233 [medium] dart's request timeout does not abort the in-flight request and does not cover the response body read
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L22-lifecycle | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: dart

The total deadline is Future.timeout around _httpClient.send(...), which only stops waiting for the response headers. The response body is then read with streamedResponse.stream.toBytes() with no deadline, so a server that sends headers and then stalls the body hangs a dart call forever. dart:io's connectionTimeout covers connect only, and idleTimeout applies to idle pooled connections, not an in-progress read. When the headers timeout fires, the underlying request is not cancelled: the socket stays open and the eventual StreamedResponse is never listened to (leaked). The other SDKs' deadlines abort the request and cover the body: go client.Timeout, node AbortSignal.timeout, rust reqwest timeout, csharp HttpClient.Timeout with buffered content, kotlin request/socket timeouts, swift resource timeout, elixir Task.shutdown, php max_duration, and the python/ruby read timeouts.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: package:http ^1.2 has no abort API. The body read can still be bounded with .timeout(), and the io client can be closed or aborted (newer package:http exposes Abortable requests), so this is not forced.

## F234 [medium] java alone retries any request, POST included, after it was fully sent (sendWithRetry), and the retry is untested
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L22-lifecycle | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: java

sendWithRetry re-sends the request once whenever the IOException message contains 'header parser received no bytes'. The comment says 'zero bytes were exchanged, so the request never reached the server'. That is wrong: the JDK raises this when the connection hits EOF before any RESPONSE bytes, after the request was written. A server that processes a POST (createPet, the OAuth2 token POST with a single-use code or a rotating refresh_token) and then drops the connection gets the request twice. The other 11 do not retry at the SDK level: python sets Retry(total=0), elixir retry:false, and go's net/http replays a non-idempotent request only when nothing was written. No test exercises the retry path.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: JDK HttpClient stale keep-alive behaviour. It can be limited to idempotent methods, or dropped to match the others.

## F235 [medium] node never consumes or cancels intermediate 3xx bodies in the redirect loop (undici connection leak); python skips release_conn on redirect-refusal paths

node's AbstractApiClient follows each Location with a new fetch() and overwrites `response` without awaiting arrayBuffer() or body.cancel() on the previous 3xx. ## F236 [medium] python redirect loop mutates the shared PoolManager.proxy_headers, so concurrent requests race and can lose proxy credentials permanently
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L22-lifecycle | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: python

_follow_redirects snapshots self._pool_manager.proxy_headers, deletes Proxy-Authorization from that shared dict on a cross-origin hop, and restores it in finally. The pool manager is shared by every request on the client, and the async facade runs requests concurrently on worker threads (asyncio.to_thread). While one request is mid-redirect, every other concurrent request through the ProxyManager goes out without Proxy-Authorization and gets a 407. Two overlapping cross-origin redirects corrupt the state for good: A snapshots {PA} and strips it, B snapshots {} (already stripped), A restores {PA}, then B restores {}, and the client loses its proxy credentials for its lifetime. No other SDK mutates shared transport state per request: java/kotlin/csharp/etc. strip Proxy-Authorization from a per-request header copy.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: urllib3's ProxyManager keeps proxy headers on the manager. Building a per-hop ProxyManager or passing per-request headers avoids the shared mutation, so this is not forced.

- `src/spec/resources/generated/python/petstore_client/default_api_client.py:736` — proxy_headers_attr.clear(); proxy_headers_attr.update(original_proxy_headers)
- `src/main/resources/templates/python/default_api_client.mustache:657` — del proxy_headers_attr[key]

buildSession uses URLSessionConfiguration.default, which has httpShouldSetCookies=true with HTTPCookieStorage.shared and urlCache=URLCache.shared with useProtocolCachePolicy. ## F238 [low] Query and form parameter order on the wire varies: insertion, hash, random, or sorted
- Status: **open** | Lens: L01-value-serializer | Category: wire | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: java, go, swift, ruby, elixir, python, rust, kotlin

For the same call, the 12 SDKs put query params on the wire in different orders. csharp, node, php, dart, kotlin (map side) and rust follow declaration (insertion) order. java collects into a `HashMap`, so the order is the hash order. go ranges over a `map[string]any`, which is randomized per iteration, so the same request can produce a different query each time. swift iterates a `[String: Any?]`, which is randomized per process. ruby is sorted alphabetically by Faraday. elixir is sorted by key (small Erlang maps). python moves every allowReserved param to the end. The Ktor transport also regroups repeated keys. deepObject sub-keys follow each language's map order, which is random in go, rust and swift. Form bodies: go sorts (`url.Values.Encode`), swift is random, java follows HashMap order, the rest use insertion order. The bytes are non-deterministic in go and swift. Use ordered containers (LinkedHashMap, slice of pairs, OrderedDictionary/array) so every SDK follows spec-declaration order.

## F239 [low] Unreserved/safe sets differ between SDKs: java and node in query values, and java, ruby and node in form bodies
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L01-value-serializer | Category: wire | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: java, node, ruby

R8-10 aligned only the OAuth2 paths to RFC 3986 `-._~`. The regular query and form encoders were left alone. Query values (non-allowReserved): csharp, python, php, dart, go, rust, swift and elixir (and ruby, after Faraday re-encodes) keep exactly `-._~` literal. java uses `URLEncoder` plus `+`→`%20`, so `*` stays literal and `~` becomes `%7E`. node uses `encodeURIComponent`, which keeps `! * ' ( )` literal (WHATWG then turns `'` into `%27`). Form bodies: csharp, python, php, dart, go, rust, swift and elixir keep `~` and send `*` as `%2A`. java (`URLEncoder`), ruby (`URI.encode_www_form`) and node (`URLSearchParams`) keep `*` and send `~` as `%7E`. I confirmed node `k=a+b%7E*%21%27%28%29`, ruby `k=a+b%7E*%21%28%29%27` and python `k=a+b~%2A%21%28%29%27`. A compliant server decodes these the same way, but the bytes differ, which matters for signing and caching. Fix by sharing one RFC 3986 unreserved encoder per language, as the OAuth2 change did.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: None

## F252 [low] Extra or missing multipart per-part headers: php adds text/plain + Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit, kotlin adds Content-Length, php Psr18 does not escape the field name

php DefaultApiClient builds multipart through Symfony FormDataPart. In the bundled symfony/mime, FormDataPart::preparePart wraps every string field in `new TextPart($value, 'utf-8', 'plain', '8bit')`, and configurePart forces encoding '8bit' on every part. So every php text part carries `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8` and `Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit`, and file and JSON parts also carry `Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit`. RFC 7578 §4.7 says senders SHOULD NOT generate Content-Transfer-Encoding. The other SDKs, including php's own Psr18ApiClient, send text parts with Content-Disposition only, so php's two transports also disagree with each other. Kotlin's Ktor formData() appends a `Content-Length: N` part header to every ByteArray part (verified from the ktor-client-core 3.5.0 bytecode), which no other SDK sends. Separately, php Psr18ApiClient interpolates the field name raw into `name="…"` without backslash-escaping `"` or `\`. Every other SDK, and php's own Symfony path, escapes it.

Reviewer suspected this is forced: php: Symfony FormDataPart's defaults. They are not forced, because Psr18ApiClient already hand-builds parts without them.

This applies to real filenames, which come from file-handle parts: java File, go *os.File, ruby/php/python file objects, node Blob.name, swift URL, elixir {:file,…}. It is distinct from the closed 'field name as filename' item. For `résumé.pdf`:
- Most SDKs emit `filename="r_sum_.pdf"`: go, rust, node and php replace per code point; java, kotlin, csharp, dart and swift per UTF-16 unit or unicode scalar.
- python emits `filename="r?sum?.pdf"` (encode('ascii', errors='replace')).
- elixir emits `r__sum__.pdf` because it replaces per BYTE.
- ruby emits NO ASCII fallback and puts the raw UTF-8 in `filename="résumé.pdf"`, which the other SDKs deliberately avoid.
- Emoji filenames produce `__` in the UTF-16 languages and `_` in the code-point languages.
The filename* value is also encoded with different safe sets. go, php, kotlin, csharp, dart, rust, python and elixir keep only `-._~`. java (URLEncoder) and ruby (encode_www_form_component) keep `*` and encode `~`. node (encodeURIComponent) keeps `! ' ( ) *`; `'`, `(`, `)` and `*` are not RFC 5987 attr-chars, and `'` is the ext-value delimiter. swift keeps the attr-char set `!#$&+^`|`. Fix: one shared rule, using the go/php buildFilenameDirective as the canonical form. Unit test: assert the exact Content-Disposition for `résumé*(1).pdf` in each language.

## F254 [low] Multipart scalar part stringification differs: python bool 'True', php bool '1'/'' and swift Int64/Int32/Float sent as application/json parts

- SDKs: python, php, swift

Scalar multipart fields are stringified differently. java (`"" + value`), kotlin (toString), go (%v), node (String()), dart ($value) and ruby (#{value}) send a boolean as `true`/`false` in a plain text part. The exceptions:
- python interpolates `{value}` in an f-string, so True becomes `True`.
- php uses strval(): true becomes `1` and false becomes `` (empty string), in both DefaultApiClient and Psr18ApiClient.

So an int64 or int32 field, which is how swift maps `format: int64`, goes to the model branch and is sent with `Content-Type: application/json`.
It is latent because the fixture's multipart companions are strings only (documentType, notes). Petstore extension: add a boolean and an int64 companion to uploadPetDocument (e.g. `isPrimary: boolean`, `pageCount: integer/int64`), and assert the exact part bytes in all 12.

## F255 [low] ruby form-urlencoded body bypasses ObjectSerializer.stringify (nil array items, Time values)
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L03-request-assembly | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: ruby

Every other SDK builds the form body field by field. It stringifies each scalar through ObjectSerializer.stringify/toFormValue and skips null array elements. Ruby instead calls `URI.encode_www_form(body.compact)`. compact only drops nil top-level fields. A nil element inside an array is still emitted (ruby 2.6 output: `tags=a&&…`, an empty pair), where java, kotlin, csharp, python, node, dart and rust skip it. Non-string scalars use Ruby's #to_s rather than the SDK wire form, so a Time becomes `2024-01-02+03%3A04%3A05+UTC`, not ISO 8601. The fixture's renewalDate is a Date, whose to_s happens to be correct. Fix: use the same explicit pair loop with ObjectSerializer.stringify that the other 11 use.

## F257 [low] A bare 'utf-16' body with a little-endian BOM decodes to garbage in csharp, swift and elixir
- Status: **fixed** (done in csharp; still open for elixir, swift) | Lens: L04-transport | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: csharp, swift, elixir

java/kotlin, python, ruby, go, dart, rust, node and php honour a BOM for a bare 'utf-16' label and default to big-endian only without one. csharp returns new UnicodeEncoding(bigEndian: true, byteOrderMark: false), which does no BOM detection. swift maps it to .utf16BigEndian; I verified that FF FE 41 00 decodes to U+FFFE U+4100. elixir passes it to :unicode.characters_to_binary(:utf16), which is big-endian with no BOM handling. A LE-BOM body therefore gives a leading U+FFFE plus byte-swapped text. A BE BOM also leaves a stray U+FEFF in csharp/swift/elixir.

- SDKs: kotlin, go

java, csharp, php, python, ruby, node, dart, rust, swift and elixir require `error` to be a non-empty JSON string, and type-check error_description and error_uri independently, setting a non-string value to null. kotlin uses `root["error"]?.jsonPrimitive?.contentOrNull`, which coerces a numeric or boolean `error` (`{"error":400}`) into the code "400", where the others report code=null and the raw-body message. The same class of coercion was fixed for refresh_token in T2-12. kotlin also calls .jsonPrimitive on description and uri: a non-primitive description throws, the catch-all fires, and the whole parse falls back to code=null and the raw body. go decodes into a struct with string fields, so any non-string description or uri makes json.Unmarshal fail and also discards a valid code. Example: `{"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":{"en":"x"}}` gives the message '…: invalid_grant' in 10 SDKs and '…: {raw body}' with code=null in kotlin and go. go additionally treats an empty description "" as absent, so the message omits ' -- ', where the others render '… -- '. This is forced only to the extent that go's getters return string, not *string.

## F272 [low] rust's per-status error wrappers render a different, context-free string from ApiError and from the other SDKs
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L05-errors | Category: message | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: rust

ApiError::from_response returns a Box holding BadRequestError, NotFoundError, ClientError and so on. Each wrapper has its own Display, for example 'Not found (404): API returned status code 404', 'Client error (418): …' or 'Network error: …'. These drop the 'HTTP status code' / 'Response headers' / 'Response body' lines that ApiError's Display (and every other SDK's string form for the same typed error) renders. ApiErrorKind adds a third format, 'API error (status N): …'. So err.to_string() for a 404 from any rust operation differs from java toString, python str, go Error() and the rest, and loses the response body in logs. Fix: have each wrapper's Display delegate to the inner ApiError's Display.

For Bearer the input is always rejected but the message differs, e.g. "\f" gives 'printable ASCII' in java and php and 'must not be empty' elsewhere. Fix: define one whitespace set, e.g. ASCII SP/HTAB/CR/LF/VT/FF or the Unicode White_Space property, and implement it explicitly per language instead of calling the native trim. ## F275 [low] In all 12 SDKs, a token that is only the 'Bearer ' prefix passes the empty-token guard and sends a credential-less Authorization header
- Status: **open** | Lens: L06-simple-auth | Category: behavior | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: java, kotlin, csharp, php, python, ruby, node, go, dart, rust, swift, elixir

The constructors reject an empty or whitespace-only token so that 'Authorization: Bearer ' is never sent. Prefix de-duplication runs later, in getAuthHeaders, so the token "Bearer " (or "bearer    ") is not whitespace-only and passes construction. Stripping the 7-char prefix then emits `Authorization: Bearer ` or `Authorization: Bearer    `, the exact unauthenticated request the guard exists to prevent. The behaviour is the same in all 12 (so not a parity gap), but the guard is ineffective in every SDK. The likely real-world case is an env var templated as `Bearer ${TOKEN}` with TOKEN unset. Fix: in every constructor, strip the prefix first and then apply the empty and ASCII checks. Unit test: `BearerAuthenticator(host, "Bearer ")` must raise 'Bearer token must not be empty'.

## F278 [low] The apiKey scheme name is pasted into each language's string literal without escaping, so legal header names can break or silently change some SDKs
- Status: **open** | Lens: L06-simple-auth | Category: codegen | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): False
- SDKs: php, node, ruby, dart, kotlin, java, csharp, python, go, rust, swift, elixir

Each Better<Lang>Codegen builds the wrapper's super-call by concatenating `spec.keyParamName()` inside a hard-coded quote character, with HTML escaping disabled: single quotes in php, node, ruby and dart; double quotes in java, kotlin, csharp, python, go, rust, swift and elixir. RFC 7230 tchar allows `'`, `$` and backquote in header and cookie names, and OpenAPI query names may contain anything. So: a header named `X-Api'Key` gives a syntax error in php, node, ruby and dart but compiles in the other 8. A name containing `$ident` becomes Dart or Kotlin string interpolation; `$apiKey` would even splice the secret into the header name. A query name containing `"` or `\` breaks the double-quote languages. The same unescaped value feeds the redirect strip-list templates. Fix: escape per target language (one helper per codegen). Extend the probe spec with an apiKey scheme whose name contains `'` and `$` so the build and lint specs exercise it.

## F279 [low] elixir omits secret fields from inspect output instead of showing '***' as the other 11 do
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L06-simple-auth | Category: api-shape | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: elixir

elixir uses `@derive {Inspect, except: [:token]}` (likewise :api_key and :password). The secret field therefore disappears from `inspect/1` output rather than appearing as a masked field. The other 11 render it as `token=***` / `apiKey: ***` / `'password' => '***'`, and their tests assert the `***` marker, which elixir's tests cannot. Secrets do not leak. Note that `inspect(auth, structs: false)` bypasses the Inspect protocol entirely and prints the raw map with the secret. A hand-written `defimpl Inspect` that emits `token: "***"` would match the other 11 and close the `structs: false` hole.

## F280 [low] go and rust auth error texts differ from the canonical strings in ways ST1005 does not require (contradicts the R8-7 'harmonised' claim)
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L06-simple-auth | Category: message | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: go, rust

Canonical texts are `API key value for 'X' must not be empty`, `Bearer token must not be empty` and `Basic auth username must not contain ...`. go wraps sentinels so the canonical phrase changes shape: `invalid API key: value for 'X' must not be empty` and `invalid bearer token: token must not be empty`. ST1005 only forbids a capitalised first word. It accepts a leading initialism such as 'API', and it would allow `bearer token must not be empty`. go's own required-parameter sentinel ('missing the required parameter ...') shows the sentinel can keep the canonical wording. go's Basic messages are canonical apart from forced lowercase. rust's BasicAuthenticator adds an extra rust-only prefix inside InvalidArgument: `invalid HTTP Basic credentials: Basic auth username must not contain ':' ...`. rust's ApiKey/Bearer and swift's Basic do not have it, and the rust test locks it in. The go bearer test asserts only the suffix 'token must not be empty', so the drift went unnoticed. Fix: use canonical (lowercased-only-where-forced) phrasing after the sentinel, and drop the rust Basic prefix.

## F282 [low] python authenticators compare and hash by value, including the secret; every other SDK except elixir and php's loose == uses identity
- Status: **fixed** | Lens: L06-simple-auth | Category: api-shape | Unit-testable (reviewer's view): True
- SDKs: python

ApiKey/Basic/Bearer (and the OAuth ones) are `@dataclass(frozen=True)` with the default `eq=True`. Two separately built authenticators with the same host and secret are therefore `==`, and they hash equal, which makes them usable as set or dict keys by value. Equality also compares the secret. java, kotlin, csharp, swift, dart, node, ruby and go (pointers) use reference identity, and rust implements no PartialEq. elixir structs (BEAM, forced) and php `==` (language, forced) are structural. python can turn value equality off with `@dataclass(frozen=True, eq=False)`, so its difference is not forced. Decide on identity (the majority) and add a test that two equal-credential authenticators are not `==`.
